problems.problem: FOUR checks in this repository asserted a literal line, a character budget, or a hard-coded count, and each went red for a change that made the atlas better: a proximity assertion measured in characters, a verifier asserting one exact statement, and three assertions saying "nine tools" that broke when a tenth was added. They are all fixed to assert the FACT rather than the characters, but nothing prevents the next one. There is no check that a check is not pinned to punctuation.

THREE times in one day a regex in a verifier of mine refused a character the data actually contains: [a-z]+ missed a family called h0, an id pattern refused a hyphen and matched ten connections of twelve, and a bus-key pattern refused an uppercase letter and matched four rows of eleven. Each reported its partial match as a whole count and passed. The pattern is a habit rather than an accident, and no check catches a check that is silently matching a subset of its subject.

SIX failure details in one day were computed unconditionally, so a failing check printed the sentence it would have printed on success. Each was found by mutation and rewritten to describe what is actually wrong. Nothing structural prevents the seventh: the ok(name, condition, detail) shape evaluates the detail whether or not the condition held, and a repository whose whole discipline rests on reading failure messages has no guard on what those messages say when they fail.

A mutation deleting a field from the RENDER left every declaration intact and the verifier green, because the check read the registry and not what reaches the reader. A second check now covers that one case. The general problem stands: most verifiers here read index.html as text, and the ones that open a browser are slow enough that they run in the manual workflow only.

Seven quantities are published by laboratories that have several stations and publish a different number in each — the spin laboratory has four and can never show all four of its thread rows at once. Those rows now name their station, verified by clicking to each in a browser. Nothing DERIVES that gating: it is declared by hand on each row, so a new station-gated publication will be silent until somebody renders it and notices.

Each measured artifact carries its own walk-time release stamp and is served with measured_on_this_release, so dated evidence is explicit rather than rewritten as current. The remaining gap is policy: nothing in the repository decides WHEN a dated artifact has drifted far enough to require an expensive re-walk.

The quantity bus publishes 257 keys and 123 of them are named nowhere but the pub() call that creates them — down from 200, closed by giving the invariant thread families that read them. A verifier holds a ceiling that only falls. The remaining ones are mostly single-laboratory internals, and no criterion says which of them SHOULD have a reader and which are legitimately private to their instrument.

the resolution laboratory puts a diffraction floor under every angle this atlas publishes, and diffraction is the only thing it models. No atmosphere, no seeing, no adaptive optics, no detector sampling, no photon noise and no exposure time — so an angle it calls resolvable may be unreachable for reasons this atlas cannot see, and the eye is already a worked example: 7 mm gives 19.8 arcsec by diffraction and human acuity is about 60, because the retina samples too coarsely to use the aperture it has. What is missing is the photon budget: whether enough light arrives in a plausible exposure. The photometry laboratory computes the flux and nothing joins the two, so the atlas can say an angle is above the floor and cannot say whether it is above the noise

a reader zooming out of the Solar System stopped at the Oort cloud because THREE separate things could decide the camera's far limit and none of them owned it: hccGo skipped entering a world whose name state.mode already carried, so the solar frame never declared its limits; stabilizeCamera then invented a ceiling of minDistance x 1e6 from a non-finite one, which for the Sun's collision radius is 131,701 AU; and a boot self-test that walks into an S3 laboratory restored the VIEW it changed but not the FRAME, leaving a solar reader with an S3 laboratory's 180 AU ceiling. All three are fixed and a late clause now asserts the promise — the frame you stand in must reach the distance where the next one takes over. What is not fixed is the shape: the limits are still set by whoever calls setControlDistanceLimits last, from every call site of setControlDistanceLimits, with no owner and no record of who decided

HCC_API.bus.counterfactual can now drive a road the atlas did not take: an admissible-but-refused coupling is appended to the link table, swept like any declared one, and removed in a finally with the path cache invalidated on both sides. For the photometer it answered that the choice of authority never mattered to the exponent — all three give exactly 1.0000, because a flux is linear in a luminosity — and mattered only to the window, twelve decades from an accretion disk against eight and a half from a supernova. What it cannot do is a counterfactual PATH: it drives one hop, and a multi-hop route whose first link is the contested one would need the route enumeration rebuilt around a link that does not exist, which is a larger change than appending one row

ten of the fourteen registries a laboratory used to be written into now come from LAB_DECLARATIONS, and a clause checks that the fold reaches each one. Four remain and they are code rather than data: a scene group, a setup function, an update call and a control panel. A declaration cannot carry those, and a table pretending to would be a worse lie than the duplication — but nothing yet enumerates them either, so a laboratory with a declaration and no update call is registered everywhere, catalogued, translated, and invisible. The liveness walk would catch it; nothing at declaration time would

a chain that is not a power law now carries the widest range over which it is one, and the rule that decides that range is |drift| <= |slope| — the same rule the verdict uses, which is why it is not tighter. It is permissive. For the white-dwarf radius the widest window it admits runs to nine tenths of a solar mass, well into where relativistic corrections are already biting, and returns -0.447 where non-relativistic degeneracy gives -1/3 and the low-third fit gives -0.3606. The window answers how far a single exponent can be stretched before this atlas stops calling it one, which is not the same question as where the physics changes, and nothing here measures the second. A tighter rule would land closer to the physics and would call fewer things laws everywhere else; the trade is stated and not made

scripts/extract-kernels.mjs read `return /^https?:/.test(x)` as a DIVISION, because its regex-or-division heuristic looks at one character and the character before that slash is the n of return. A phantom regex then swallowed four lines including an `if(...){`, the brace was never counted, and the parser's depth went to -1 and never recovered — so every declaration in the last ten thousand lines of index.html was invisible to extraction, and naming one as a root reported that it is not a top-level declaration: a true sentence about the parse and a false one about the file. Keywords are read as words now and the balance is checked at the line where it breaks. What stays open is that this parser is a heuristic at all: it is not a JavaScript parser, and the next construct it misreads will be found the same way this one was, by someone being told a function that is plainly there does not exist

the Reeb station's linking number is a 512x512 Gauss double integral, and the operational-forecast audit was paying it 128 times per laboratory — pfInverseRoots scans the control at 128 points and bisects each bracket, building the whole diagnostics object every time to read ONE cheap number out of it. Making that one field lazy took pspGauss from 1449 ms to 52 ms of boot self time. The fault is not fixed, only one instance of it is: no laboratory DECLARES which of its outputs are expensive, so nothing distinguishes a solver that reads one arithmetic field from one that reads a quadrature, and the next expensive field added to any diagnostics object will be paid for by every caller that never looks at it

the boot suite now has two tiers and scripts/selftest.mjs holds reader mode to a 4.5 s budget and a 60 per cent floor on the assertions it keeps, but the floor is a stated number rather than a measured property: nothing checks that the clauses reader mode KEEPS are the ones whose subject is the document in front of the reader. the photon station drew Poisson counts from the linear congruential generator this atlas uses in a dozen places — seed = (seed*1103515245 + 12345) & 0x7fffffff — and the drawn mean came out 12.8 sigma low at lambda = 12 and 21.4 sigma low at lambda = 25, because Knuth's method multiplies a run of uniforms together and the low bits of an LCG are not independent enough to survive that product. That station uses mulberry32 now and checks itself. What is NOT fixed is everywhere else: the same recurrence still seeds asteroid belts, star fields, sampled walks and at least one self-test, and none of those draws is checked against the distribution it is supposed to have. A generator good enough to scatter points is not good enough to be measured, and nothing here records which of the two each use needs

the equation of state splits its Fermi-Dirac quadrature at the edge of the Fermi surface, and I wrote into the laboratory that a uniform grid of the same size comes out half a per cent low. It does not. Solved end to end each on its own grid, a uniform rule at the same 840 nodes is accurate to three parts in ten million; the half per cent I measured came from pairing a degeneracy parameter solved on one grid with a pressure evaluated on another, which is a mistake of mine and not of Simpson`s. The split does earn its place — thousands of times better at the degenerate states — and at a THIRD of the budget it is worse than the rule it replaces, which is now checked too. What stays open is the general case: every numerical choice in this atlas is justified by a comparison at the setting it was tuned at, and nothing sweeps the setting to find where the choice inverts. A rule tested only where it wins has not been tested

the timescale laboratory published a doubling time in YEARS that had been multiplied by the number of seconds in a year: M/Mdot with a mass in solar masses and a rate in solar masses per year is already in years, and converting it again hid a factor of thirty million behind an expression that reads correctly. It was caught by a self-test asserting that a hundred million solar masses eating one a year doubles in a hundred million years, not by anything structural. NOTHING IN THIS ATLAS CHECKS THAT AN OUTPUT`S VALUE IS IN THE UNIT ITS DECLARATION NAMES. The quantity bus checks that two declarations agree with each other, which is a different thing entirely: two laboratories that are both wrong by the same factor couple happily, and the transfer sweep measures a slope that is right while the magnitude is not. Every unit label here is a promise nobody verifies

for ninety-five releases this atlas published five solid angles, six magnitudes and two arcseconds, and no instrument consumed any of them: an entire per-solid-angle dimension existed in the outputs and in no input, and nothing reported that. The unit census that finds this is a script somebody runs by hand while writing a laboratory, not a gate — api/manifest.json publishes the isolated INSTRUMENTS and never the isolated UNITS, so a quantity every laboratory can produce and none can take is invisible to every check here. Surface brightness closed this one. The general fault is open: nothing measures the supply and demand of the atlas`s own units, and the next orphan dimension will be found the same way this one was, by a person looking

LAB_DECLARATIONS was built so that a laboratory is declared once and every registry reads it, and it works exactly as far as somebody remembered to write the spread. The astro rows of PREMIUM_VIEW_DOMAINS and NEXUS_CLUSTERS carried labDeclIn and the quantum rows did not, so the first declared laboratory outside the astro cluster landed in no visual domain and no cluster at all, and five separate clauses reported it at once. The fold`s own check verifies that every DECLARED laboratory reaches ten registries; it cannot verify that a registry not yet spread into would have accepted one, because until a declaration lands outside the cluster somebody happened to test with, the gap is invisible. Two spreads were added. The category key was wrong in the same edit for a different reason — the declaration said quantum where the rendered registry says quant — and nothing relates the two vocabularies either

the frequency-coincidence census decides commensurability from the fractional part of a ratio, and above 2^53 every double IS an integer, so the fractional part comes back as exactly zero and the census called the pair commensurate. Adding an information bound of order 1e50 beside a phonon at 1e13 produced thirty-four spurious commensurabilities in one release. Such pairs are refused as unresolvable now and counted separately. What stays open is the class: this atlas spans forty-one decades of length and a hundred and twenty of information, and EVERY comparison it makes between two quantities from opposite ends of that range is one subtraction away from the same fault. Nothing audits the atlas`s own arithmetic for range, and the next instance will be found the way this one was — by a number arriving that is further from its neighbours than a double can carry a fraction

a reader reported that the dropdown lists close without letting you choose. I found a real defect — the panel rebuilds by innerHTML and a rebuild while a list is open destroys it — deferred buildCtl while a select holds focus, wrote a check that a focused select survives a buildCtl, watched it pass, and shipped. The lists still closed. The rebuild that kills the popup does not arrive through buildCtl at all: the panel DEFERS renders while a control is held and FLUSHES them on pointerup, and for a select pointerup is when the popup OPENS, not when the interaction ends. The check I wrote exercised the fix I had made rather than the fault the reader hit, so it could not have failed for the reason it existed. It is now driven through the real path — pointerdown, a render queued behind it, pointerup — and was watched going red with the fix reverted. What stays open is the class: this suite has nine hundred and fifty assertions and nothing distinguishes one that reproduces a reported failure from one that restates an implementation, and a check of the second kind is worth nothing at the moment it matters most

the kernel-extraction check greps the extracted module for browser globals, and it has now been wrong twice in opposite directions. First it matched the bare word and failed on the string `stop = window` written as a literal; tightened to require a dereference, it failed on the sentence `twice the window. It is published so...` inside a doc string, where the full stop after the word is punctuation and not a property access. It now strips string literals, template literals and comments before grepping, and that is proven both ways -- it no longer fires on the prose, and it still catches a real window., document., requestAnimationFrame( and new MutationObserver. What is NOT fixed is the general case. This atlas is written as long English inside string literals, and every other check that greps a source file is exposed to the same confusion; the fix was applied to the one check that failed, and nothing surveys the rest. A regular expression cannot tell code from prose, and this file is mostly prose

ATLAS_BUS.pub(key, value, unit) names its third parameter `unit`, and across roughly two hundred call sites that parameter holds `cos(theta/2)`, `to E2`, `recede`, `1-Tc/Th`, `l(l+1)` and `x Phi_0` as often as it holds J or rad or W. It is a display caption -- what to print after the number -- and it is named as though it were a dimension. That naming is why the invariant thread could put a Lyapunov exponent per unit time beside one per iteration for as long as it did: anything reading the bus for units would have been reading prose, so nothing read it, so nothing checked. The thread now declares its own units per row and the boot assertion measures those, which fixes the thread and not the bus. Renaming the parameter is a four-consumer change and was not made, because the honest name is neither `unit` nor `caption`: the field is a unit where one exists and a caption where none does, and the atlas has no way to say which it is on any given call

the open problem above was filed when the predictability horizon declared inputs called `steps` and `tolerance` and the bus proposed three meaningless couplings. It closed by saying nothing stops the next laboratory from calling an input `n` or `count` or `eps`. The next laboratory was the clock exchange, written in the same session by the same hand with that paragraph already on the page, and it declared an input called `neighbours` -- whereupon the bus proposed a coupling from the 600-cell, whose vertices have neighbours too. One laboratory, and the prediction came true; it was renamed to `fit_window`. And then a THIRD time, in the release immediately after the base rate below was measured and published: the cosmological-constant laboratory declared an output called `radius_ratio` and the bus proposed a coupling into an accretion disk`s radius ratio. Three laboratories, three collisions, every one of them written by somebody who had just finished writing about the hazard. What is now known that was not then is the SIZE of the hazard rather than its existence -- a third of the bus, wrong twice as often -- and that no filter can be built because the correct dimensionless couplings outnumber any rule that would exclude the wrong ones. So this stays open as a discipline and not as a defect: every proposal must be answered in writing, and the only thing that has ever caught one of these is somebody reading it

the quantity bus admits a coupling when the unit string agrees AND the coordinate name agrees, and where the unit is dimensionless the first condition is vacuous: the name carries the whole proposal. That was filed twice as a prediction and is now MEASURED. Thirty-one of eighty-three admissible candidates rest on a name alone and eighteen of them are refused -- fifty-eight per cent -- against twenty-nine per cent for the fifty-two that carry a dimension. Exactly twice as wrong. Fifty input and output names in this atlas are used by three or more laboratories and a dozen of those are single letters. What the measurement also settled is that NO MECHANICAL RULE FIXES IT, which is why none was built: refusing dimensionless proposals would break thirteen correct and load-bearing couplings, among them the mixmaster anisotropies into three laboratories; refusing generic names would not help, because `redshift` is as specific as a name gets and is refused twice. The decisive case is a name admissible into two laboratories where one coupling is declared and the other refused -- same output, same name, same absent unit, different answer -- and what separates them is physics. The base rate is published in the manifest and the written refusal is the only thing doing the work

the dropdown lists took three attempts because each fix reached a different link of one chain and none of them reached the first. The panel`s accordion WRAPS every section by relocating its children into a body div, and the phone layout REORDERS sections by re-appending them through a fragment; both re-parent nodes, and moving a focused element blurs it. The blur releases the render the panel was holding, the release rebuilds the panel, and the rebuild destroys the element the open popup belonged to. Chrome names the mechanism in as many words when the following removal fails — Perhaps it was moved in a blur event handler? — and I had read that message twice before understanding it. Both movers are guarded now and the invariant is checked against every one of the ten functions that touch this panel. What stays open is that the invariant is enforced one caller at a time: nothing prevents an eleventh from re-parenting a focused control, and the guard is a habit each of them has to remember rather than a property of the panel

the doctrine of this atlas is two authorities for one fact, and the exoplanet laboratory is the first case where the SECOND one was the one that was wrong. The independent verifier computed the four Kopparapu habitable-zone bounds as sqrt(L / S_eff) where the atlas computes bound_AU * sqrt(L / L_sun), and the two forms are not the same thing: the four numbers 0.75, 0.97, 1.70 and 1.77 are DISTANCES in astronomical units for a star of one solar luminosity, and their reciprocal squares are the effective fluxes. Dividing by them instead of multiplying put the early-Mars bound INSIDE the recent-Venus one, which inverts the zone and is not visibly absurd in a single printed number -- it took the disagreement with the atlas to expose it. What was learned is that a second authority is a DISAGREEMENT DETECTOR and not a referee: it says the two differ and it never says which is right, and the only thing that settled it was working the physics a third time by hand. The boot assertion now checks the ORDER of the four bounds rather than their values, because an inverted zone passes every check written on magnitudes alone. What stays open is sharper than it first looked, and it has now been measured. There are eighty-six verifiers, and TWENTY-EIGHT of them read the atlas at all -- eighteen through the extracted kernels, seven through index.html, seven through a published artifact. THE OTHER FIFTY-EIGHT NEVER READ IT. They implement the physics independently and check it against itself, which is a valuable statement of what ought to be true and is NOT a second authority on this atlas, because there is no comparison step in them for a disagreement to surface through. That was demonstrated rather than argued: corrupting the Stefan-Boltzmann exponent from 4 to 3 in api/sensitivity.json is caught immediately by verify-measured-exponents, which reads that file, while verify-photometry and verify-timescales pass unchanged at 7/7 and 11/11, because a broken atlas is invisible to a file that never opens it. So the doctrine of two authorities buys what it promises for twenty-eight of these and something weaker for the rest, and the original worry -- that a verifier might be wrong in a way that agrees with the code -- turns out to be the smaller problem. The larger one is that most of them cannot agree or disagree with the code at all. AND THE ARTIFACTS ARE WATCHED TWO DIFFERENT WAYS, which was also measured. Of the eight published artifacts, four are read by a verifier that asserts properties of their content -- the manifest, reach, sensitivity and transfers -- and four are guarded only by REPRODUCTION: liveness.json, openapi.json, open-problems.json and the agent report are regenerated and diffed against what is committed. Those two mechanisms fail differently and neither subsumes the other. Reproduction catches a stale or hand-edited file exactly, and is blind to a WRONG GENERATOR, because a generator that is wrong today produces the same wrong answer twice and the diff comes back clean. Assertion catches wrong content, and is blind to whatever nobody thought to test. So the four artifacts under reproduction alone have no check at all on whether the thing writing them is right. What is still unmeasured is the original question for the twenty-eight verifiers that do compare: an error made twice by the same hand agrees with itself, and nothing here would notice

the holographic census asks whether each holder on the information rail sits near its own bound, and "near" is written as occupancy greater than one half. Occupancy goes as one over R squared, so that check tolerates a radius wrong by a factor of 1.41 in either direction before it notices anything: dropping the 2 from the Schwarzschild radius quarters the bound and moves the black hole from 0.99 of it to 3.96, which is still "near the bound" to any comparison and is caught only by the separate EQUALITY that the black hole sits on its own bound to twelve figures. The equality was nearly worthless as written, because it first computed the radius itself instead of asking ilHolderRadius -- the function the rail is actually drawn with -- so a wrong radius in the drawing would have passed a check that recomputed the right one beside it. That is fixed. What stays open is general: this atlas is full of checks written as comparisons against a threshold, and for any quantity that depends on its input to a power the tolerated error is the threshold taken to one over that power. ONE HALF OF THIS IS NOW SPENT: the inventory exists. scripts/sensitivity.mjs already sweeps every declared input of every instrument and fits a log-log slope to each response, and that slope IS the power the tolerance arithmetic needs -- so the amplification is one over its absolute value, computable for all 430 clean couplings the atlas publishes. It is checked in docs/verify-measured-exponents.cjs, which also turns the sweep from something merely produced into something falsifiable: the measured slopes reproduce Wien at -1, Stefan-Boltzmann at 4, the Planck peak at 5, Hawking at -1, the horizon area and entropy at 2 where a volume law would give 3, evaporation at 3, Kepler and the Jeans mass both at 3/2, and signal-to-noise at the square root of the exposure. 318 of 365 clean fits land on an exact integer or half-integer, which is a fact about the physics and not about the fitting. The blindest coupling is the photovoltaic concentration against its open-circuit voltage at a slope of 0.021, where a ten per cent band on the output permits an eighty-nine-fold error in the input. WHAT REMAINS OPEN is the other half: nothing yet connects that inventory to the ASSERTIONS. Knowing that a quantity goes as the inverse square does not by itself find the boot check that tests it against a threshold, because the assertions are prose and code rather than declarations naming the quantity they bound, and no mechanical path leads from one to the other

the quantity bus admits a coupling on two tests -- the units must convert, and the two quantities must be the SAME COORDINATE -- and the second test reads quantity_kind, a field carried by seventy of the atlas`s one thousand three hundred and seventy-seven declared outputs. Where that field WOULD be decisive is the fifty-seven declared couplings, because each one is a hand-made, reviewed statement with a written reason that two particular things are the same coordinate. Three of the fifty-seven name it at both ends. Fifty-four name it at neither. AND NOT ONE NAMES IT AT EXACTLY ONE END, which is the number that decides what can be done: there is nothing to inherit, nothing to propagate, and no shortcut. Populating them means NAMING the shared coordinate for each coupling one at a time -- and that is the first honest way to fill this field that has been found, because it records a decision the atlas already made and defended rather than guessing from a name, which is the mistake this register already carries twice. WHY IT IS NOT DONE IN THE RELEASE THAT MEASURED IT: hccQuantityCompatible treats two unset kinds as compatible, so giving one end of a pair a kind while the other has none converts a coupling the bus currently ADMITS into one it refuses. Fifty-four couplings and their neighbours would move at once, the admissible-coupling census would shift, and the boot assertion that every admissible proposal is either declared or refused in writing would have to be re-satisfied against a different set. That cascade is real work and wants its own release rather than being smuggled into a measurement. CLOSED IN v4.211.0, AND THE CASCADE WAS REAL. The forty connected components of the coupling graph were each given one name, applied at registration from a single table so the provenance stays visible -- these kinds came from the couplings and not from what a field is called. Outputs carrying a kind went from 70 to 118, inputs from 21 to 80, distinct kinds from 30 to 61. THE FIRST ATTEMPT SPLIT TWENTY-THREE ADMISSIBLE PAIRS, exactly as this entry predicted: kinding one end of a pair and not the other converts a coupling the bus admits into one it refuses, and the admissible set fell from 91 to 68. Twenty-two of the twenty-three were the same coordinate reached from only one side and were restored by naming the other end -- among them a flux arriving beside an exitance leaving, which the first naming had split into two names without anybody deciding to. ONE WAS NOT RESTORED AND IS THE FINDING: imp.beta and skyrmion.beta share a name, a unit and admissibility, and this atlas refused that coupling in writing years ago because one is the magnitude of a reflection coefficient and the other is a skyrmion parameter. Giving the second the same kind would contradict a decision already argued, so it has none, and the pair now fails the KIND test before it ever reaches the written refusal. The prose became structure and the sentence stays, because it is the only place a reader learns why

the exoplanet laboratory declared a transit depth in parts per million and the same depth in per cent BOTH as dimensionless, and they differ by exactly ten thousand at every system it carries -- two outputs of one quantity, in one declared unit, of which at most one declaration could have been right and neither was. It was found by hand and the obvious next move was a GENERAL detector: for every instrument, any two outputs sharing a declared unit whose ratio is constant across several settings are two spellings of one quantity. THAT DETECTOR WAS BUILT AND IT IS NOT SOUND, and the attempt is written down rather than the detector shipped. Its first form reported twenty pairs and most were two numbers that never moved at all, because a constant ratio proves nothing when both quantities are constant -- fixed by requiring each output to take at least two distinct values. Its second form reported eight, and the ones that survived were mostly a residual near machine epsilon in the denominator, which makes any numerator look like a huge constant multiple. The one that looked most like a real find was osc.wavelength_vacuum over osc.wavelength_air, 874030 in one declared metre, and it is CORRECT: they are the electromagnetic and the acoustic wavelength at one kilohertz, and their ratio is the speed of light over the speed of sound. A check that cannot tell that pair from the exoplanet pair would have shipped a false accusation about working physics on every run, which is worse than the gap it closes. What would make it sound is a way to say that two outputs are the same MEASUREMENT and not merely the same dimension -- the quantity-kind field is exactly that and is unset on most outputs, so the honest order is to populate quantity_kind first and only then ask this question of pairs that share one. CLOSED IN v4.212.0. The prerequisite this entry named -- populate quantity_kind first -- was met at v4.211.0 by naming the forty coordinates the declared couplings had already argued for, taking the field from seventy outputs to a hundred and eighteen. The detector is written now and restricted to pairs that share a declared KIND as well as a declared unit, which is exactly what separates the exoplanet depth in ppm beside the same depth in per cent from the vacuum wavelength beside the acoustic one: the wavelengths share a metre and neither carries a kind, so the check cannot speak about them and does not. IT IS NEARLY BLIND AND IT PRINTS ITS REACH BESIDE ITS VERDICT, because a check that finds nothing because it cannot see is not the same as one that finds nothing because there is nothing, and only the second is good news. Measured on the release that shipped it: it compared ninety-one pairs and found none, could not speak about three thousand four hundred and ninety more that share a unit and lack a kind on one side or both, and excluded fifty-one that share a unit and declare DIFFERENT kinds -- which is the test doing its job rather than failing to. It sharpens exactly as far as the kinds are named, and no further

v4.213.0 measured the nesting and drew it, and v4.215.0 made it askable over HTTP with its one knob, the margin — and inside the page the census stood at margin one and nowhere else. A reader could see a number and could not see what the number depends on, which for a census whose whole point is that the declared extents are the shakiest values in the catalogue is the wrong half of the finding. CLOSED IN v4.216.0: the margin is a slider, the containment lines rebuild live from it, the readout beside it is written from the census at the margin the slider is at, and every placed object can be coloured by its measured depth — a small whole number, so the scale carries no interpolation and no normalisation. The measurement that makes the slider trustworthy is monotonicity: growing every declared radius can only ADD a containment, so the count must rise at every step of a sweep, and that is asserted at boot and in the verifier. It runs 9 containments at margin 0.3 to 110 at 2.5, and we ourselves are inside nothing below 0.615

the chain runs local -> galactic -> Local Group -> cosmic web, and BOTH galaxy models were cut at the last step: a reader zooming out from the Local Group watched the Milky Way and Andromeda blink out of existence exactly as the cosmic web appeared, and coming back in Andromeda vanished again one layer earlier. The atlas states the opposite principle twelve lines away in the same function, about the Oort cloud staying visible from the galactic frames so that leaving the Solar System is a continuous nesting and never a light-switch, and the two galaxies were the one place that principle was not applied. CLOSED IN v4.218.0: both are kept from the galactic layer to the top of the chain, where they shrink to motes because a galaxy beside a gigalightyear IS a mote, and Andromeda gets the bounded angular marker the Milky Way already had so it stays findable rather than merely small. Found by a reader looking at the screen, which is the only instrument that finds this class of defect

the phase-space frame pointed its camera at the world origin and its subject stood at (0, 4, -26), so the torus a reader opened that frame to see was always up and behind the view. The cause is one line: the torus is a CHILD of the resonance web, deliberately, and the framing read its .position -- an offset inside that web, zero -- as if it were a world coordinate. CLOSED IN v4.218.0 at both ends: the offset is cancelled where the parent is stood down, so the torus is genuinely centred on its own stage, AND the framing asks for a world position, so the two can never disagree again whatever it is parented to. THE GENERAL FAULT IS FILED, NOT THE PARTICULAR FIX: every other frame handler in that function reads a .position the same way, and any of them whose instrument is ever re-parented will fail identically and silently

CLOSED IN v4.220.0 without guessing anything, and the entry is kept because the way it closed is the point. the collision that started this — two cycle instruments at (0,-13,-24) — is one case of a general defect: a stage assigns coordinates to its instruments one at a time over releases and two of them collide, and nothing reveals it unless some frame happens to show both. So the question is asked of the WHOLE SCENE: sibling groups that both declare a non-zero position and declare the same one. It walks 583 sibling groups across 41 stages and returns twelve. MOST OF THE TWELVE ARE CORRECT. The Giant Ring, the Giant Arc and the Big Ring are three fields declared at the same right ascension, declination and redshift because that is where the paper puts all three; the Coma members are drawn at the cluster distance on purpose. A co-location is a defect when the coordinates were hand-assigned to a stage and correct when they come from a catalogue that says so, and the census cannot tell those apart BECAUSE THE GROUPS IT WALKS ARE ALMOST ALL UNNAMED. So the number is reported and nothing is asserted from it, and the one assertion made is scoped to the cycles instruments, where every position is a hand-assigned stage coordinate and the discrimination is free. WHAT CLOSED IT was not naming groups by guessing which are instruments — that would have been the same mistake one level up — but reading the declarations the atlas already had. Every catalogue entry computes its position from a declared right ascension, declination and distance, so it says placedBy:catalogue; every cycle instrument takes its position from the frame table by hand, so it says placedBy:stage. Nothing was invented. The eleven co-locations resolve to six the catalogue declares, ZERO between hand-placed instruments, and five still unidentified — a ceiling that only falls, held by the boot suite, which will fall further as more of the scene declares where its positions come from. v4.221.0 took the last five to ZERO the same way: the Nexus refusal strikes and family hubs are placed at a midpoint and a centroid of a graph layout, so they declare placedBy:computed and two of them coinciding is what the layout says; and the Andromeda far marker added in v4.218.0 stands on the Andromeda model on purpose, both from one catalogued coordinate. All eleven co-locations are now accounted for — seven catalogue, four layout, ZERO collisions — and 215 of 698 groups are named with 200 declaring an origin, floors that only rise. THE CEILING FELL TWELVE TO FIVE TO ZERO ACROSS THREE RELEASES AND NEVER ONCE BY LOOKING HARDER: every step was a declaration of where a position comes from

the thirteen cycle frames each show one or two instruments, and the coordinates they stand at were assigned one at a time as each was written. Two of them were IDENTICAL -- the reference-plane instrument and the chronometry observatory both sat at (0, -13, -24) -- and no frame revealed it because no frame ever showed them together. CLOSED IN v4.218.0 by a frame that shows all twelve at once, with an arrangement that is DERIVED rather than chosen: the rows are the groups the atlas already declares, an instrument sits in the row of the first frame that shows it, and every gap, between columns and between rows alike, is the sum of the two measured bounding radii plus one margin. The first version typed the row gap as 34 and the clearance check caught it at 0.977 -- the galactic butterfly, radius 25, reaching into the row in front of it -- so the row gap is measured too. The boot suite reports the closest pair on the stage and fails if any two touch

the scale comparator has quoted the Virgo Supercluster, the BOSS Great Wall and the Huge-LQG as sizes since long before any of this, and the catalogue could not put a marker on one of them. v4.213.0 pinned a ceiling of 320 on the RAW count of refused containment overlaps, on the doctrine that a ceiling only falls. Placing seven structures the atlas had been naming and could not point at took it to 389 — not because anything got worse, but because six of the seven have a field midpoint for a centroid. The container-level count was no better: fifteen of thirty-eight became eighteen of forty-five for the same reason. A pin that makes the atlas refuse to place a known object in order to keep a number down is the exact inversion of what a pin is for. CLOSED IN v4.216.0 by moving the pin rather than raising it: the raw counts are published as OBSERVATIONS, and what is pinned is the thing honest work cannot raise — every container the census refuses must say, in its own words, WHY. It is zero and zero is the only value it may take. Two containers were found not to say it and were given the reason: the Hercules-Corona Borealis excess has no centre to know, being a point process defined by a significance test, and the Eridanus supervoid`s centre is a density minimum whose position moves with the void-finder. THE GENERAL LESSON IS FILED, NOT THE PARTICULAR FIX: this register holds several ceilings, and any of them that counts a population rather than a defect has the same fault

with the Local Supercluster placed, the containment census puts the observer OUTSIDE it: our distance to the Virgo Cluster is 0.0540 gigalightyears and half the most-cited diameter of the supercluster centred on it is 0.0538. That is not a discovery. It is two uncertain numbers landing on top of each other, and the honest report is the closeness rather than the verdict — a hundredth of a per cent of margin flips it, and the atlas now has a slider that shows exactly that. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT is a sourced diameter with its membership criterion stated: published figures run from about 33 megaparsecs on the classical de Vaucouleurs membership to over 50 on looser ones, and a row that said which it meant would make the verdict mean something. Until then the atlas reports the number and the width of the doubt, and does not choose

this atlas has drawn shells on a three-sphere since it began — last-scattering screens, horizon spheres, the curvature-radius family — and could never say WHAT A SHELL CAN AND CANNOT TELL YOU. CLOSED IN v4.226.0 by implementing Preece & Batenin (9 September 2026) as arithmetic rather than quoting it as a result. A band through degree L holds N_L = (L+1)(L+2)(2L+3)/6 field directions; q sky maps of it leave exactly N(L−q) unidentifiable so long as the observation commutes with rotations about the observer, and no angular resolution buys one of them back. L+1 distinct non-polar shells are necessary AND sufficient, and there is a design that attains that minimum with every singular value exactly one. A resolved layer of half-width epsilon is injective and pays for it: its weakest squared singular value falls as epsilon^(2L). A SINGLE MAP HAS EXACTLY ZERO LOCAL FISHER INFORMATION ABOUT ITS OWN ANGULAR RADIUS once an unrestricted positive band spectrum is profiled out, and TWO calibrated shells recover the curvature radius from their highest sector alone, without the field and without the band power. The verifier reproduces the paper`s own printed coefficient table to the last printed digit, its exact shell ranks for 0 <= L <= 8, its degeneracy test at chi = 0.9, and its two-shell inversion at d1 = 3, d2 = 6, R = 10 — twenty-one checks against numbers printed in a document this atlas did not write

v4.231.0 aliased `m s^-1` to `m/s` with a comment saying that a second table entry would be a second authority for one metre per second — and in the same release added `J s` as a second row while `J·s` was already in the table. One unit, two entries, one release after the sentence forbidding it. CLOSED IN v4.233.0 by removing the row and aliasing the spelling, and the class is pinned: no two entries of the conversion table are one unit under two spellings. IT WAS FOUND THE SAME WAY THE QUANTITY-KIND COLLISION WAS, by normalising every string and counting, which is the argument for the census rather than for more care. AND THE TWO NORMALISERS DIFFER IN ONE RESPECT THAT MATTERS: the kind normaliser lowercases and the unit normaliser must NOT. MeV and meV are both declared, they are a megaelectronvolt and a millielectronvolt, they differ by a factor of a thousand million, and a case-insensitive unit check would call them one unit. The separators are ignored; the case never is

the bus admits a coupling on two tests and the second compares the quantity KIND as a string, so a coordinate spelled two ways is two coordinates as far as the bus is concerned and two publications of one physical quantity are silently refused. Nothing errors, nothing warns, the link simply never appears — the defect`s whole signature is an ABSENCE, which is why only a census could find it. It had happened once: `density` in kilograms per cubic metre was declared `mass density` in one laboratory and `mass_density` in three. CLOSED IN v4.232.0 by spelling it the way the other three do, and the class is pinned at zero: sixty-three kind strings normalise to sixty-three coordinates, and the number that collapse is nought. AND TWO PAIRS THAT NORMALISE APART ARE KEPT APART ON PURPOSE, with the reason written beside them, because a reader who sees them side by side will otherwise merge them: a speed is the magnitude of a velocity and has discarded the direction, so routing a dispersion into a terminal speed must stay impossible; and a nat of information differs from an entropy by Boltzmann`s constant and by what is being counted, and this atlas holds both kinds of laboratory. Ten coordinates are used exactly once and couple with nothing, which is reported rather than pinned, because that is a fact about the catalogue and not a defect

v4.248.0 gave the atlas a COUNT — twenty-nine independent dimensionless groups — and a count is not a list. v4.249.0 computes the list exactly over the integers and then does the harder thing: it says what the list IS NOT. BUCKINGHAM IS A NECESSARY CONDITION AND NOT A SUFFICIENT ONE: the theorem says any physical law relating these quantities must be expressible in their dimensionless groups, and it does NOT say every dimensionless group is a law — nothing in dimensional analysis could ever say so. A group is a DIRECTION IN WHICH A RELATION COULD EXIST, and this atlas refuses to call one a discovery. SORTED, THE TWENTY-NINE COME APART INTO THREE DIFFERENT THINGS: twelve NAMED laws, which are linearly independent and therefore span twelve of the twenty-nine and no fewer; five DEFINITIONAL identities, each touching at most two kinds — area over length squared, volume over length cubed, information — which say one kind IS a power of another, and counting those as discoveries would be counting the metre twice; and twelve COMPOUND directions of three or more distinct kinds with no name in this atlas. Each compound group is drawn in the lattice as a CLOSED LOOP, because a dimensionless group is exactly a walk through the exponent lattice that returns to the origin and seeing it close is seeing why it is dimensionless — drawn dim and unlabelled on purpose, since drawing a candidate as boldly as E = mc² would make a claim the theorem cannot support. AND THE BASIS IS A CHOICE WHILE THE DIMENSION IS NOT: the boot suite permutes the columns, re-runs the elimination, and checks that every basis vector changes while the count changes by nothing — because reporting a basis as though it were canonical is the commonest way to make linear algebra lie

eighty-three convertible units across thirty-four quantity kinds, each carrying a NAME and a conversion factor and not one of them carrying a DIMENSION. So the atlas could say two quantities were both lengths and could not answer the question that turns a set of quantities into a physics: WHICH COMBINATIONS OF THEM ARE DIMENSIONLESS? CLOSED IN v4.248.0 by giving every KIND — never every unit, because a dimension beside a unit would be a second authority for one physical quantity — its exponent vector over the seven SI base dimensions, after which the answer is linear algebra: the dimensionless combinations are the null space of the dimension matrix and by rank-nullity there are exactly n − rank of them. MEASURED ON THE ATLAS`S OWN QUANTITIES: n = 34, rank = 5, so TWENTY-NINE independent dimensionless groups are formable from what the instrument already carries, and two of the seven base dimensions — amount of substance and luminous intensity — are used by NOTHING in it, which is a fact about this instrument rather than about the SI. A π-ENGINE THAT CANNOT REDISCOVER KNOWN PHYSICS IS NOT ONE, so twelve laws are required to appear in the null space from dimensions alone — E = mc², E = hν, PV = E, TS = E, P = IA, Φ = BA, p = mv, a = v/t, ρ = m/V, u = E/V, V = E/q and j = q/At — and four combinations that are NOT dimensionless are required to fail, each differing from a real law by exactly one factor. AND THE THEOREM REPORTS WHAT DIMENSIONS CANNOT SEE, which is the most useful thing it can say about this atlas: three pairs of kinds the file keeps carefully apart have IDENTICAL dimensions — intensity and radiance, inverse time and frequency, energy density and pressure — so dimensional analysis alone can never justify routing one into the other, and exactly one kind sits at the origin because a bit is a pure number. The lattice is drawn in the Field Lab on the three axes that carry almost everything, with current and temperature MARKED rather than dropped silently, and coincident kinds drawn as one dot with both names — which is the thing a table of units cannot show. The lattice and the field solver take the world in turn from one place, because the solver rewrites its own visibility and its own caption every frame and hiding its pieces would be a second authority arguing with the first sixteen times a second

the holographic panel scope asked for in the design brief — cyan #00f0ff, gold #ffaa00, violet #b026ff — was MEASURED AGAINST WCAG BEFORE IT WAS APPLIED rather than after, which is the only order in which a threshold decides anything. Against the panel ground (rgba(4,7,14,.92) composited over #02040a, which is #04070e, because a translucent panel is not its own colour) the relative-luminance formula gives cyan 14.31:1 and gold 10.56:1, both clearing AA body text — and VIOLET 4.38:1, which FAILS the 4.5 body text needs while clearing the 3.0 a UI component needs. So the violet appears only in chrome, in an inset ring and a chip outline, and never in a text colour; where violet text is wanted there is a second token which is the SAME hue lightened in linear space by the LEAST factor that clears 4.5 — 1.0578, giving #b527ff at 4.51:1 with the hue moving 1.3°. Solving for the least factor rather than picking a lighter purple is what keeps it the same violet, and the check proves the margin is minimal by showing that one per cent less lightening fails. ADDED IN v4.247.0 as a THIRD OPT-IN SCOPE alongside Obsidian rather than as a replacement, because the tokens at :root are read by three separate mechanisms and overwriting one to change a look has bitten this file before; removing the attribute restores every value :root declares, and one line sets the scope so there is never a second authority for which look is on. The blur is conditional on @supports for the same reason Obsidian`s is: a panel that turns transparent where the browser cannot blur is worse than a plain one. AND THE BOOT CHECK FOR THIS WAS WRITTEN WITH `|| true` ON THE END, the third time in this run of releases — which is the argument for the mutation pass rather than for more care

every view in this atlas was an orbit about a point somebody else chose. That is the right default for a scientific instrument, and it meant the reader could never go and STAND somewhere: inside the cosmic web, between the Hopf fibres, off to one side of the Galaxy — all of it orbitable and none of it enterable. ADDED IN v4.246.0 as three properties, each measured on the live camera in the boot suite. FRAME-RATE INDEPENDENCE: velocity is in world units per SECOND and thrust, decay and displacement all integrate against dt, so under constant acceleration eight steps of 2dt cover EXACTLY four times eight steps of dt — a camera that moves per frame fails that and nothing else in the file would notice. THE DAMPER IS CHECKED AGAINST ITS OWN EXACT SOLUTION rather than against the idealisation it does not implement: the scheme decays then steps, so its travel is v₀·dt·q/(1−q) with q = exp(−dt/τ), which is 0.475% short of the continuous v₀τ at dt = 4 ms — the first version of the check compared against v₀τ and went red by exactly that discretisation, which is a real number to REPORT rather than a tolerance to absorb. And the verifier`s own first draft carried 0.417986 as a typed constant beside the formula and went red by 1.7e-5, so it now runs the integrator and compares. THE CEILING: the rule that a world`s reach is bounded by the radius of what it draws was written for the zoom, and a flight mode that ignored it would reopen the void that rule closed, so flight is clamped by the same zoomCeilingNow(). THAT CHECK WAS ALSO WRONG FIRST — it flew outward for fifteen seconds from wherever the reader was and never got near the limit, because the target is carried a fixed distance ahead so the speed scale never grows; a mutation removing the clamp went undetected. It now starts just inside the ceiling, which is where a clamp either works or does not. Speed scales with the reader`s own distance from what they are looking at, so one control works in astronomical units and in hundreds of gigalightyears without a units panel

every orbit was a LineBasicMaterial at one flat opacity: a closed curve saying where a planet goes and nothing whatever about HOW it goes there. The single most famous fact about an orbit — that a body moves fastest at perihelion and slowest at aphelion, which is Kepler`s second law and the reason his first two were worth writing down — was drawn nowhere. CLOSED IN v4.245.0, and the speed was already in the loop: the energy integral of the two-body problem gives v² = μ(2/r − 1/a) and r = a(1 − e cos E) is computed at every vertex of the curve already, so it costs one square root per point. In AU and years about this Sun μ = 4π², which follows from the definition of the astronomical unit rather than from a fit, and Earth comes out at 29.785 km/s against a measured 29.78. THE RATIO THE COLOUR SPANS IS AN IDENTITY, NOT A NORMALISATION: at the apses the velocity is perpendicular to the radius so v_p r_p = v_a r_a, hence v_p/v_a = (1+e)/(1−e) EXACTLY, held to four parts in 10¹⁶ over every planet — so the brightest and dimmest points of every trail stand in a ratio fixed by the eccentricity alone, Mercury`s spanning 1.518 and Earth`s 1.034, and a near-circular orbit draws a near-uniform line BECAUSE it is near-circular. AND THE COLOUR ENCODES THE THING THAT IS NOT CONSERVED while the checks hold the one that is: h = √(μa(1−e²)) is constant and h = r v sin φ recovers it at every point of every curve, which is the whole content of the second law. μ itself is controlled by a law it was not chosen from — P = 2π√(a³/μ) reduces to √(a³) in years only if μ = 4π². Each trail keeps its own body colour at aphelion and warms toward perihelion, so the planet stays recognisable and the variation is the physics

a reader looked at the S³ section, saw the observable cap with `observer p` at its middle, and asked whether the zoom-out chain should end THERE rather than at the origin of the projection. It should, and it did not: both legs of the Observable ↔ S³ seam read controls.target.set(0,0,0), which is the centre of the three-sphere — a point no chain of scales leads to and nobody has ever been. Coming out of our own observable Universe should put you where our own observable Universe IS. CLOSED IN v4.244.0. The atlas already knew where that is: the cap is drawn at geodesic radius χ_P about the +Y pole and its passport returns (0, RU, 0), so one function reads that point and nothing else writes a second one down. AND THE MAP ACROSS THE SEAM IS NOW STATED AS WHAT IT IS — a SIMILARITY. The Observable world is observer-centred at one unit per gigalightyear and the carrier is one unit per hundred, so p ↦ O + p/100: a translation composed with a uniform scale, which preserves every distance RATIO and every ANGLE in the scene exactly and changes only which point is the origin. That is strictly stronger than the radius being preserved, and the reader`s own position is the fixed point of the map, which is the whole reason to anchor it there. THE SAME RELEASE PUT ONE SWITCH AT THE BOTTOM OF THE CONTROL PANEL for every automatic move between scales — the rungs of the solar ladder, the hand-off out to the Observable Universe and back, and the hand-off on to the carrier and back. Five places, governed separately or not at all, so a reader who wanted the instrument to stop moving them had no single way to say so. It is appended after the per-mode body, so it is at the bottom of the panel in every world rather than only in the one where somebody remembered to put it. AND THE CHECK ON IT WAS WRONG FIRST: it counted how many times state.scaleChain appeared beside false and asked for five, but the checkbox`s own render is one of those, so deleting a real gate left four gates and five matches and the check stayed green. A mutation proved it. Each of the five transitions is now named and looked for where it actually lives

the Milky Way band was fifteen hundred Gaussian blobs at H*0.034 with a bulge at W*0.15 — numbers with no relation to any galaxy. What a person actually sees looking up is the LINE-OF-SIGHT INTEGRAL through the disc they are standing in, and every quantity that integral needs has been measured: h_R = 2.6 kpc, h_z = 0.30 kpc, R₀ = 8.178 kpc from GRAVITY 2019, dust scale height 0.125 kpc, 1.8 mag/kpc of V extinction in the plane at the Sun. CLOSED IN v4.243.0: the brightness toward Sagittarius, the width of the band at each longitude and the fall-off with latitude are now consequences of one expression rather than three separately tuned constants, and the axis ratio h_R/h_z = 8.67 is the whole reason the Galaxy is a BAND. THE SHARPEST FINDING IS ABOUT THE DUST AND IT WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: with the extinction coefficient pinned by its own definition — κ·ρ_dust(R₀,0) = 1.8/1.0857 per kpc, so κ = 38.5 and no other value — a SMOOTH exponential dust disc gives I(ℓ=0)/I(ℓ=180) = 1.01 and no band at all, because only the nearest half kiloparsec survives and that is nearly isotropic; while no dust at all gives 45:1, which is far too much. The band exists because real dust is in CLOUDS covering a small fraction of sight lines, which is why Baade`s Window exists, so the smooth law is applied at a declared covering fraction and 0.05 returns 5.15:1 with an 8° half-width toward the centre, both inside the observed range. The fraction is a stand-in for structure the model does not resolve and is written down as one rather than folded into κ. The drawn dust clouds use the DUST scale height rather than the stellar one, which is why the rift lies inside the band and cuts the bulge instead of bounding it

this atlas has placed every physical scale at its level N = ln(R/ℓ_P)/ln φ on the golden ladder since it was built, and had NEVER ASKED THE QUESTION THAT PLACEMENT INVITES: do the rungs mean anything? If the ladder were a law rather than a coordinate, scales would cluster on its integer rungs and the fractional parts of N would not be uniform — and the offsets are points on a circle, so the Rayleigh test applies exactly: R = |Σ exp(2πi u)|/K with p = exp(−K R²) under the null, no free parameter anywhere in it. ADDED IN v4.242.0, AND THE ANSWER IS NO: over the atlas`s own 113 placed scales the golden ladder returns R = 0.135 and p = 0.129 against a threshold of 0.01 written down before the measurement. THE CONTROL IS SHARPER THAN A NULL RESULT USUALLY IS — run the same test on the same scales against base π and it returns p = 0.118, very slightly BETTER than φ; base e gives 0.66, base 2 gives 0.77, base 10 gives 0.68. A first draft of the comment claimed φ led the five, and the live catalogue said π does, by a margin that is itself meaningless, which is exactly the point. The golden ladder is a COORDINATE AND NOT A LAW. A DETECTOR THAT CANNOT FIRE IS NOT A DETECTOR, so three controls run in the boot suite every time the atlas opens: offsets clustered on a rung return p ≈ 2e-37, offsets clustered exactly BETWEEN rungs return p ≈ 8e-35 — it detects any concentration and not only the flattering one — and uniform draws return p ≈ 0.73. The spectrum is drawn as a CIRCULAR histogram because the quantity tested is an angle, where a bar chart would split any cluster straddling a rung across opposite ends of the picture and hide it, and the resultant is drawn at length R so the statistic is visible without reading the number. The catalogue is walked from PHI_ATLAS itself, so a scale added to the atlas enters the test without anyone remembering to add it

Harmonices Mundi, 1619, Book V: the ratios of the planets` motions are musical. Kepler had the intervals right and no way to sound them, and this instrument had the same ratios in its own element table and no sound at all. ADDED IN v4.241.0. The frequency IS the orbit: a planet whose mean longitude advances at `rate` degrees per Julian century completes 360° in 36000/rate years, so f = rate/(36000·365.25·86400) hertz and nothing else is needed — the same rates the orbits are drawn from, never a second table of periods. Mercury is 1.3157e-7 Hz and Pluto 1.2781e-10: the real pitch of the solar system, and TEN OCTAVES of it, which is why no single transposition can work — put Pluto at 55 Hz and Mercury lands at 72 kilohertz. Each voice is therefore multiplied by its OWN power of two, always an integer, until it lands between 220 and 440 Hz. That is octave equivalence, which is what a musician means by an interval, and it leaves every ratio exact modulo factors of two — held by a check that a non-integer fold fails immediately. WHAT YOU HEAR IS THE RESONANCE STRUCTURE: Jupiter against Saturn is 2.4824, the 5:2 great inequality to 0.70%, and Neptune against Pluto is 1.5045, the 3:2 mean-motion resonance they are actually locked in, to 0.30% — and the check proves it can tell those from non-resonances by measuring Earth:Mars and Venus:Earth, which are near nothing. Level and stereo place come from where each planet actually is relative to the camera rather than from a preset, and a planet that is not being drawn is silent. NOTHING SOUNDS UNTIL A READER ASKS, and off means the context is CLOSED rather than muted, because a silent oscillator is still an oscillator. The verifier`s own first run reported intervals between 31 and 32 instead of between Mercury and Venus: a spread of {hz, n} into a record whose name field was also `n` replaced every planet`s name with its octave count, which is a key collision with no error attached

this laboratory has run a photon around a great circle of S³ since it was built, and the reader had only ever watched it from OUTSIDE — from a vantage that does not exist, in a space that has no outside. The one view this instrument can offer that no other can is the view from the photon, and it was the one view it did not have. ADDED IN v4.240.0 as three exact statements, each checked. The heading is the tangent and a tangent to a geodesic is orthogonal to the position EVERYWHERE: |p·t|/|p| ≤ 8e-17 over a full circuit, and it is taken from the closed form rather than differenced between frames, because a heading built from two frames wobbles with the frame rate. The antipode arrives at arc π and is a PLACE: after 1722.6 Gyr the rider is at −p, the point every geodesic leaving the start reaches at once, which is exactly why Γ reaches one there and not before. And the circuit closes at 2π, 3445.2 Gyr, back to the start within 1e-15 of a unit with no wall passed, because ∂S³_R = ∅ — the closure is the whole point of the model and had never been something a reader could experience rather than read. TWO THINGS ARE HIDDEN FOR THE DURATION AND BOTH ARE STATEMENTS: the carrier surface, because a surface you are ON cannot be in front of you, and the observable cap, because from inside a region you see its boundary and not its fill — the cap is 4.8° across and the ride begins at its centre, so filled it covered the entire forward hemisphere. Riding fixes where the camera is and not where it looks: the orbit target sits a short way along the tangent, so a drag turns the head in the seat. AND THE CHECK ON Γ WAS WRONG TWICE, IN THE SAME DIRECTION BOTH TIMES: first it asked for Γ(π/2) < ½ when Γ(π/2) is EXACTLY ½ and the real content is the identity Γ(χ) + Γ(π−χ) = 1; then it asked for Γ(0.99π) < 0.9999 when it is already 0.9999934, because Γ approaches one CUBICALLY as 1 − 2ε³/3π. Both times a guessed inequality was hiding an exact statement, and both are now the exact statement

bloom, SMAA and a tone map, and then the image went to the screen as though it had been captured by nothing at all. Every real instrument that has recorded this sky puts three things into the picture and all three are LAWS rather than looks. ADDED IN v4.239.0. Natural vignetting is exactly cos⁴θ and the exponent is derived rather than dialled — one cosine from the foreshortened aperture, one from the foreshortened sensor element, two from the inverse square of the longer oblique path — so at a 55° vertical field the corner falls to 0.221 on 16:9, 0.133 on 21:9 and 0.421 on 1:1, purely because the corner ANGLE is a function of the aspect. The field angle is therefore taken from the projection matrix rather than from the screen radius, and one shader is right at every aspect instead of at the one it was written on; one function computes it and both the frame and the boot suite call that function, because a check that recomputes what it is checking is checking its own arithmetic. Grain is photon shot noise: arrivals are Poisson, σ = √N, so absolute grain grows as √L while grain RELATIVE to the signal falls as 1/√L and therefore lives in the shadows — the uniform overlay almost every film-grain shader uses has that law exactly backwards and looks like dirt on the glass. Lateral colour is zero on the optical axis and linear in field height with the channels in wavelength order, because a lens focuses short wavelengths at a different magnification; a constant RGB offset across the whole frame, the other thing almost every shader does, is not aberration at all. TWO NUMBERS ARE KEPT APART ON PURPOSE: the exponent, which the optics gives, and the FRACTION of the law that is drawn, which is a display choice — a real lens is corrected in the barrel and again in software, and a fifth of the frame at a fifth of the brightness is a photograph rather than an instrument. And the whole pass is fenced: it runs on the display buffer after tone mapping, only under premium visuals, and no number the atlas reports passes through it

the planets were MeshStandardMaterial with a single hex colour and nothing else — Earth a blue ball, Venus a beige one, Mars an orange one, and not one of them carrying the shell of air that is the reason any of those colours is what it is. CLOSED IN v4.238.0 by deriving rather than painting: hydrostatic balance against the ideal gas law gives H = RT/(μg), so the file carries T, μ and g — published per body — and the scale height appears nowhere as a constant. It lands on the published heights: Venus 15.90 against 15.9, Earth 8.43 against 8.5, Mars 10.83 against 11.1, Uranus 26.98 against 27.7, worst 13% at Saturn, which is what an ISOTHERMAL scale height deserves when the real atmosphere is not isothermal. The colour is Rayleigh in one line, σ ∝ λ⁻⁴, giving 0.428 : 1.000 : 2.441 across the sRGB primaries so blue scatters 5.705 times as hard as red — exactly (680/440)⁴ — with the Rayleigh phase ¾(1+cos²θ) and a Henyey-Greenstein lobe for the hazy ones, lit from where the Sun actually is rather than from wherever the camera happens to be. WHAT IS DRAWN IS EXAGGERATED AND SAYS BY HOW MUCH: eight scale heights of Earth air is one per cent of its radius and of Jupiter`s three tenths of one per cent, so the drawn thickness is a compressive but STRICTLY MONOTONE function of the true ratio — Titan still has the deepest air and Jupiter the shallowest — and the factor, 2.1 to 9.7, is reported per planet. AND WHERE THERE IS NO AIR NOTHING IS DRAWN: Mercury`s surface-bounded exosphere has no fluid to take a scale height of, Pluto`s nitrogen freezes onto the ground as it recedes so one H would describe it at one point in its orbit only, and both refusals are written down, because a body with no shell and a body nobody got round to are indistinguishable on a screen. One of those reasons was first written too short to be a reason and the boot suite`s own length floor caught it

a reader looked at the Hopf laboratory and asked how precisely the innermost fibres land on the centre of the whole projection. EXACTLY, and the closed form says so in one line: at θ = 0 the fibre is the unit circle about the origin — radius sec(0) = 1, centre tan(0)·(−sinφ, cosφ, 0) = the origin, normal the polar axis — and for EVERY φ, because at the pole of the base sphere there is one point and φ is degenerate there. All three come out to the last bit. The family spirals onto it at a known rate: R − 1 = θ²/8 and |C| = θ/2, so the centre offset outruns the radius change by 4/θ, and at the innermost ring the laboratory draws, θ = 0.25, that is sixteen to one — which is exactly why the knot at the middle of the picture is as tight as it looks. THE COMPLEMENTARY LIMIT IS HELD TOO: as θ → π the fibre passes through the pole of the stereographic projection, R and |C| both diverge, and R − |C| = 1/(R + √(R²−1)) → 0, so the circle straightens into a LINE — and the coaxial invariant R² − |C|² = 1 is exactly what forces that. Neither degenerate limit is swept as a tube and the laboratory draws neither: its rings run 0.25 to 1.85. The unit circle IS now drawn, once, as a declared reference, because it is the axis the whole bundle winds around and a reader who can see it can see what every other fibre is doing. ADDED IN v4.238.0, and the first version of the straightening check carried a 2 where the algebra gives a 1, which the check caught against the closed form it was written from

the atlas opens on the Sun, and the Sun was a MeshBasicMaterial at 0xfff2c4 edge to edge with a radial-gradient sprite behind it — no limb, no surface, no corona, and the one thing anybody can check by looking, that it is a BALL and not a disc, was what the drawing threw away. CLOSED IN v4.237.0 by deriving it rather than painting it: in a grey atmosphere under the Eddington approximation S(τ) = ¾F(τ+⅔), so I(μ)/I(1) = (2+3μ)/5 and the limb is 0.400 of the centre, against an observed visible 0.3 to 0.4; and because radiation leaving at angle μ comes from optical depth τ ≈ μ, the same approximation gives T(μ) = T_eff·(¾(μ+⅔))^¼ — 6103 K at the centre and 4854 K at the limb, against a textbook limb of 4800 to 5000 K. So the edge is REDDER as well as dimmer, by an amount the file computes, using the very same Planck-through-the-CIE-observer chain that colours the two hundred thousand stars behind it. THE IDENTITY THAT KEEPS IT HONEST is the disc integral: 2∫I(μ)μdμ / I(1) = 4/5 exactly, so a limb-darkened disc radiates precisely what a uniform disc of its mean brightness would and the model cannot secretly brighten or dim the star. The corona is Baumbach 1937 / Allen`s published K+F profile, whose three terms each own the range they were measured for and which spans more than three decades between 1.03 and 3 solar radii — which is why a corona drawn at any single opacity had always looked wrong. THREE FAULTS IN THE FIX ARE RECORDED IN IT. The corona was first a sphere, so the camera was routinely inside it and the back-face additive shell washed the whole screen; an optically thin halo is the integral along the line of sight, which for a spherical halo is a function of PROJECTED radius alone, so it is a billboard and the inside/outside problem stops existing. That billboard was then parented to the SPINNING star, so copying the camera`s orientation into it did not face it at the camera and the corona lay across the disc as a dark ellipse. And the limb colour ladder came back BLACK: the buffer carried three bytes per texel while the texture was RGBA. The diagnosis was wrong the first time and the mutation test corrected it — putting the removed THREE.RGBFormat constant back does not fail a format check at all, because the DataTexture constructor takes RGBAFormat as its default and silently repairs undefined. Only the buffer LENGTH can catch it, so that is what the check reads. The Sun rendered black and nothing reported an error; it was invisible only because a bright sprite sat in front of it

every fibre in the Hopf laboratory was a THREE.Line: one hundred and sixty samples of the parameterisation joined by one-pixel segments at one flat opacity. A polyline has no surface, so it has no normal, so it can carry no light and no thickness that survives being looked at edge-on — and the CROSSINGS, which are the entire point of a laboratory about linking, were the place the drawing was thinnest. CLOSED IN v4.236.0 by deriving the closed form: stereographic projection takes circles on S³ to circles in R³, and the fibre over (θ,φ) projects to radius sec(θ/2), centre tan(θ/2)·(−sinφ, cosφ, 0), normal (−sin(θ/2)cosφ, −sin(θ/2)sinφ, cos(θ/2)) — derived here rather than looked up, and checked against the parameterisation the beads still slide along, which it matches to 3e-12 with the whole remaining gap accounted for by that function`s 1e-9 pole guard and held against the bound the guard`s own size implies. TWO EXACT INVARIANTS FALL OUT AND ARE PINNED RELATIVELY: R² − |C|² = 1 for every fibre, so the whole family is coaxial with the unit sphere, and C·n = 0, so each centre lies in the plane of the circle it centres. The claim the laboratory exists to make is now COMPUTED rather than captioned: the Gauss double integral returns 1 for every pair of distinct fibres and 0 against a circle that is not one of them, because a measurement that cannot tell linked from unlinked is not a measurement. The bundle is one merged swept mesh whose frame is written down rather than transported — for a circle the outward radial direction and the plane normal already close on themselves after one turn — and the light running along each tube is the S¹ action the Hopf map quotients by, on the same clock as the beads. AND THE FIRST TUBES WERE UNREADABLE, WHICH IS ARITHMETIC AND NOT TASTE: additive blending sums every surface along the ray, seventy-eight fibres are six to ten tubes deep near the centre of the projection, and at the brightness one line wants the sum saturated the whole frame to white — the bundle was there and none of its structure was. Each tube now emits a fraction of what it would alone, only front faces are drawn, and the rim dispersion is declared in the file as the cheat it is rather than presented as physics

a reader reported that zooming out of the Solar System past the giant-structure shells cut the picture to black — the mode tab switched to the Observable Universe exactly as it should, and there was nothing to look at. SCALE_SEAMS CORRECTED THE SEAM AND THE BLACK SCREEN SURVIVED IT: measured on a flicked wheel after that fix, six consecutive frames in the cosmic layer at 5.06e16 AU with 84 of 5184 sampled pixels lit. A hand-off cannot save a reader it never gets a frame to run in. The other half was that every world`s zoom ceiling was a number typed beside it with no relation to how far out that world`s farthest object actually is: walked from the scene graph, the cosmic layer let the reader fly SEVENTEEN TIMES past the last thing in it, the field lab ten, the cycles four; and the compact S³ world kept its outermost surface three times OUTSIDE its own ceiling, so nobody had ever been able to back off far enough to see all of it. OrbitControls dollies multiplicatively with no per-frame bound, so one flick crossed the whole emptiness between two frames. CLOSED IN v4.235.0 by deriving every ceiling from the radius of what the world actually draws — never nearer than 1.15 times it, so no world is too big to see, and never further than three times it, so no world can empty, except a rung of the solar ladder that has a rung above it — and by bounding the dolly to 2.6 times per frame, which limits the rate and never the reach and gives every seam a frame to act in. The hand-off also goes through the router now, so the breadcrumb can no longer read Solar System over a picture of the Observable Universe. TWO OF THE THREE FAULTS WERE IN THE FIX ITSELF AND ARE RECORDED: the rate bound wrote its answer into the variable it then tested against, so it computed the right number every frame and never moved the camera; and re-deriving the ceiling every half second measured the CAMERA rather than the world, because several markers are sized to hold a constant angular size and grow with distance — the cosmic ceiling climbed 8.7e15 → 2.2e16 → 5.1e16 over six frames of one flick, walking the reader back into the void the rule exists to close. The re-measurement now runs only from inside the content, where that loop has no gain. AND THE GUARD ASKED ITS OWN SUBJECT FOR PERMISSION: the first check read the exempt list out of the rule it was guarding, so adding the cosmic web to that list restored the entire void and the check stayed green. The exempt set is derived from the ladder now — exactly the rungs with a successor — and that mutation fails. Measured after: the darkest frame of the same flick went from 84 lit pixels to 411, and it is no longer in the cosmic layer at all

the backdrop behind every view in this instrument was nine thousand four hundred points of one flat slate blue at one fixed size. It is the most looked-at surface in the file and it was the least examined. CLOSED IN v4.234.0 by computing each star`s colour from Planck`s law against the CIE 1931 observer at load, from h, c and k, with no table of colours in the file to drift from the physics — checked against a published blackbody table, which is an authority outside this repository, to within ten parts in 255 across 1000 to 30000 K and within two at the Sun. THE FIRST VERSION OF THE POPULATION WAS WRONG AND THE CHECK CAUGHT IT: drawing masses straight from Kroupa`s initial mass function put 3.5% of the sky above 10000 K where the solar neighbourhood has about 0.1%, because the IMF describes what was BORN and massive stars leave. Weighting by the fraction of the disc`s age each mass survives lands the drawn sky on the observed census — 80% M dwarfs, one star in thirteen hundred above 10000 K — and that correction is now itself pinned by a check that removes it and measures the damage. The sky is 204 000 stars because the spectrum is integrated 256 times onto a grid the code builds from the law rather than once per star, and the grid is required to agree with the law it came from to under one step of an eight-bit channel. WHAT IS STILL NOT PHYSICS IS SAID SO: the positions are random and declared random, the sizes compress a million-to-one luminosity range and declare the compression while keeping its order, and the twinkle is atmospheric rather than stellar, bounded, and switched off for a reader who has asked for reduced motion

the atlas carried "1252 outputs without a quantity kind" as one debt for many releases and it is THREE debts wanting three different things. Sorted in v4.231.0: 346 outputs have a unit the atlas can convert and need only a coordinate name; 916 are honestly pure numbers, where a kind needs evidence of a different sort; 125 are refused with written reasons; and 35 hold PROSE in the unit field, which is the only one of the four that is a defect and was invisible inside the total. A census of every spelling found 169 outputs in 42 spellings the atlas had declared NOWHERE — neither convertible nor refused.
