Ten of those were ordinary SI and are now declared with exact factors (the elementary charge and the reduced Planck constant as SI defining constants, one nat as one over ln 2 bits, the Hubble unit as a reciprocal time); two were one unit spelled two ways and are aliased; the rest are classified, each with its reason. THE SHARPEST FINDINGS: fifteen outputs said their unit was `text`, which names a TYPE and not a scale, so those outputs are strings and were never numbers; four said `length`, `length/time`, `1/length` or `momentum`, which names a DIMENSION and withholds the unit — the distance ladder`s own defect one level up; and TWO held a pipe-separated list of permitted answers, which is a value domain saying what the output may BE rather than what it is measured in. The pin is that nothing is unclassified, because a spelling nobody has classified is a spelling nobody has read

the tomography could say which field directions a set of sky maps loses and could not say what losing them costs, and the two are not the same sentence. CLOSED IN v4.230.0. For Gaussian noise of positive-definite covariance the Fisher matrix is T*N^-1 T, so its kernel IS the kernel of T: two fields differing by a null direction of amplitude a have IDENTICAL data distributions, and for any estimator the larger of their two mean squared errors is at least a^2, because the average of two risks equals the risk about their midpoint plus a^2. No cleverness removes that and no prior removes it without adding information from outside. Where q has reached L+1 nothing is null, and the floor is returned as NOTHING rather than as a zero that would read like a bound. The resolved layer has the companion statement: its weakest direction carries a Cramer-Rao variance of sigma^2 over lambda_min and therefore grows as epsilon^(-2L), so halving a layer at L = 3 multiplies that variance by sixty-four exactly. The atlas now publishes the cost beside the count

the shell-tomography paper devotes a section to what defeats its own reconstruction, and three releases had implemented only what it achieves. CLOSED IN v4.229.0. A JET IS WORTH SHELLS EXACTLY: measuring normal derivatives of orders 0 through s−1 at ONE radius imposes a root of multiplicity s on each radial polynomial and leaves the same N(L−s) directions unidentifiable that s distinct shells would — verified over 0 <= L <= 6, the range the paper checks its own confluent ranks. THE LEAKAGE BOUND is the paper`s (eta2 + g eta1)/(1 − eta1) and it REFUSES to return a number at eta1 >= 1, where the identity gives none. THE NEARLY-FLAT EXPANSION is checked by its own departure, which scales as K^2 with a constant that holds across four decades of curvature — the O(K^2) term the paper writes and does not evaluate. AND THREE OBSTRUCTIONS ARE DECLARED BECAUSE NO COMPUTATION REMOVES THEM: an unknown relative gain b makes the observable b g(R), so one ratio cannot determine two parameters; source evolution between two light-cone shells is the same problem wearing a physical name; and distances obtained by assuming the curvature under test return the assumption. An instrument that carries the positive results without the conditions under which they fail is worse than one that carries neither

v4.226.0 implemented the shell-tomography paper as arithmetic and reported it as text. Three of its four results are SHAPES and had no picture: the thin-layer spectrum is a ladder of L+1 rungs at the powers epsilon^(2k) with multiplicities (L−k+1)^2; the two-shell ratio is a strictly monotone curve, and its monotonicity is exactly why one measured ratio gives one radius; and the exact statistical degeneracy is two rows of bars of which one moves and the other does not. CLOSED IN v4.228.0 by drawing all three from the same functions the readout uses rather than from a sketch of them, so a picture cannot drift from the number beside it. AND WHAT THE SCENE CONTAINS IS NOW ASKABLE — the census builds the group on demand and counts its shells, curves and captions, because a theorem with no picture and a picture with no theorem are both easy to ship and only a count tells them apart

the atlas draws six observer-centred screens — the surface of last scattering, the particle horizon, the event horizon, the light-travel sphere, the acceleration onset and matter-radiation equality. Each one IS a sky map, so from v4.227.0 each carries the exact per-shell verdict: at band L it sees (L+1)^2 of the N_L directions and loses N(L−1), whatever its angular resolution. That part is sound and is appended in the ONE constructor every such shell goes through, so a screen added later cannot arrive without it. THE JOINT NUMBER IS COMPUTED AND REFUSED. Six shells would exhaust a band through degree four, which is a reading a viewer of six nested spheres could very easily take, and it is wrong: they are maps of different fields at different epochs — a photon decoupling surface, a causal boundary, a curvature candidate — not q maps of one field on one slice, and the paper is explicit that source evolution, line-of-sight integrals, lensing and selection must be in a forward model first. The bound is published with joint_claimed:false beside it, because computing a number and refusing it is a different act from not computing it

the cap fraction f(chi) = (chi − sin chi cos chi)/pi is computed in the tomography laboratory for exactly one reason: to say that it is NOT an information fraction. It does not determine the rank of a sky-transfer operator, nor its noise-conditioned singular values, and analytic continuation from an open volume does not imply continuation from one embedded two-sphere — the explicit kernel P_q(cos theta) H_(<=L−q) is a counterexample. THE ENTRY IS OPEN RATHER THAN CLOSED because the atlas elsewhere draws volume fractions and geodesic-ball fractions in contexts where a reader could take them for information content, and no census yet measures where. What would close it is a walk over every published fraction asking what it is a fraction OF

six outputs of the distance ladder are lengths and every one of them declared unit dimensionless, with its own doc string saying in parsecs, in light years, in megaparsecs. Nothing had noticed because nothing had asked: the unit census measures PUBLICATIONS and these six are contract outputs that the ladder does not publish. CLOSED IN v4.225.0 — pc, ly, pc, Mpc, pc, pc, each with quantity_kind length — and the light year was added to the unit table on the way, defined as the gigalightyear the table had held for releases divided by a billion rather than typed a second time. AND TWO PUBLICATIONS THE LADDER HAD BEEN MAKING FOR RELEASES WERE DECLARED IN NO CONTRACT AT ALL: rungs.hubble_constant_late and rungs.hubble_constant_early went onto the bus and could not be routed. It became visible the moment a THIRD Hubble constant arrived — localflow.hubble_constant, fitted from the atlas`s own galaxies in v4.224.0 — and the three could not be compared, because two were not declared to exist and the third declared no kind. All three carry quantity_kind hubble_rate now, which is what lets the bus say they are the same measurement rather than merely the same unit. Unrouted publications 167 to 165, routable 103 to 138, kinded outputs 118 to 161, and every pin pulled down onto the measurement

the atlas has quoted a late-time Hubble constant up its own distance ladder for releases, as a CALIBRATION, and has held forty-five galaxies at exact positions with published distances since v4.213.0. The two had never met. CLOSED IN v4.224.0: twenty-four of those galaxies now carry a measured radial velocity, and a velocity against a distance is the Hubble law with nothing else in it. Fitted through the origin — the law has no intercept, and adding one would quietly absorb the very infall the fit exists to show — it returns 72.5 km/s/Mpc from twenty galaxies with a scatter of 438 km/s. THE DEVIATIONS ARE THE PHYSICS AND THEY WERE NOT PUT IN BY HAND. Dropping the four Virgo members raises the fit to 73.7 and lowers the scatter to 292: the cluster`s own mass decelerating the flow around it. The single largest residual is M86 at minus fifteen hundred kilometres a second, and M86`s own catalogue entry, written three releases earlier for a different reason, says it is falling through Virgo at 1500 km/s toward us. The fit was never told that. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: twenty galaxies are not a cosmological sample and this is not a measurement of H0. The agreement with the quoted value is a check on the catalogue, not evidence about the Universe, and the laboratory says so in its own limits

v4.213.0 placed forty-five galaxies at exact J2000 positions and published distances, and every use the atlas made of them was descriptive: draw them, count what contains them, report the census. CLOSED IN v4.215.0 with the first thing done with the catalogue that is a PREDICTION. Every other galaxy recedes; M31 approaches at 110 km/s, and it can only be approaching because the pair turned around and fell back, which happens if and only if there is enough mass. Kahn & Woltjer 1959 turns that into one equation in one unknown, and solved with the atlas`s own separation (M31`s own catalogue entry), its own declared approach speed and its own model age — nothing typed in the laboratory at all — it returns 4.285e12 solar masses against roughly a twentieth of that in stars. The missing-mass problem one rung above a rotation curve

the timing argument gives the Local Group 4.285e12 solar masses; the zero-velocity surface, measured at 0.96 Mpc, gives 1.74e12 with the cosmological constant carried exactly. Both are computed here from the same age and the same Lambda and the ratio is PUBLISHED rather than reconciled, because it is a real disagreement in the literature and not an artefact of this implementation. WHAT WOULD NARROW IT, and is not done here: the timing argument as coded is the Lambda = 0 cycloid, because carrying Lambda through a radial two-body orbit needs a second numerical solve; published treatments put that correction near a tenth, which does not close a factor of two and a half. The size of Lambda IS shown, on the estimator that carries it — dropping it moves 1.74e12 down to 1.276e12 — so a reader can weigh it rather than take it on trust

declaring the Local Group timing argument made gyro.age -> localgroup.age admissible on the instant: gyrochronology returns an age in gigayears called age, the timing argument takes an age in gigayears called age, the units convert and the coordinate names are identical. BOTH TESTS THE BUS RUNS PASSED, and the coupling would have let a four-billion-year-old star decide how much mass the Local Group has. It is refused in writing rather than the check being loosened, and the entry stands because it is the first demonstration that the two-test rule is necessary and NOT SUFFICIENT — the atlas has believed the pair of tests enough to admit ninety couplings on them. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT is a scope on a quantity kind: an age of one object is not an age of the whole history, and nothing in the vocabulary says so. Adding that distinction by guessing which of the existing kinds are scoped would be the same mistake one level up

the atlas states a length in three places. PHI_ATLAS is the zoom ladder, a hundred and thirteen rows from the Planck length to the full S3 circumference. SCALE_REFS is the comparator the fractal bench reads to say what a scale is about the size of. COSMOS is the catalogue that draws the structures at real positions. Seventeen subjects appear in two of them at once and nothing had ever compared the two numbers. CLOSED IN v4.214.0 by comparing them: eleven agreed to within two per cent and ten to within half, which is exactly the argument for doing it — a number typed twice and agreeing today can disagree tomorrow with nothing in the atlas to notice. Thirteen rows no longer hold a number at all; they hold the authority that already existed, and the metre in a gigalightyear is read from the unit table rather than typed beside them. WHAT REMAINS OPEN is that the pairing is DECLARED and not discovered: seventeen rows were matched by subject, by hand, and a length written twice under two unlike names is not in the census at all. Seventeen is a floor on the finding, not a bound

the South Pole Wall stood in the scale comparator at 1.37e25 metres against the catalogue`s 1.296e25 — a ratio of 1.0570, which is 10^25 divided by 9.4607e24 to five figures. It was one point three seven gigalightyears converted with a ROUND gigalightyear. CLOSED IN v4.214.0, and the reason it is worth a register entry rather than a quiet edit is that it was PROVABLE: the disagreement carried the signature of the mistake that made it, so nothing had to be decided. The boot suite now asserts that the atlas`s own unit table gives 9.4607304725808e24 and that a round 10^25 would be 5.70% high, so the same conversion cannot be made again without a red check

Laniakea stood in the zoom ladder at 2.5e24 metres against the catalogue`s 4.92e24 — a ratio of 0.508, a radius under a name that means diameter everywhere else. CLOSED IN v4.214.0, and the reason it could be repaired rather than only declared is EVIDENCE AND NOT TASTE: two authorities to one. The catalogue gives 0.52 gigalightyears across and the scale comparator independently gives 4.9e24 metres, which is 0.518, and the row`s own note calls it our basin of attraction — the basin, not half of it. Repairing it moved five ladder rungs, Laniakea rising past the Bootes void and the BAO ruler, which is what a factor of two does and is the visible proof the repair was not cosmetic

Virgo, Coma, the Great Attractor and Shapley are each stated twice and disagree by factors of 1.8, 3.1, 1.6 and 5.9, and they are DELIBERATELY NOT REPAIRED. Each has exactly one authority on each side, and the two are measuring different things: a virial radius against a drawn diameter, a dense core against a whole supercluster complex. Shapley is out by 5.9, which no radius-and-diameter confusion produces. Choosing a winner between two defensible definitions would be inventing a measurement rather than making one. WHAT WOULD CLOSE EACH is the same thing in four places: a stated MEASURE KIND on the row — radius, diameter or length — quoted from the source the row came from, at which point the two numbers can be compared as like with like or shown to be about different objects. The atlas has no such field today, and adding one that is filled in by guessing would be the same mistake one level up

for twenty-one releases this atlas held forty-eight clusters, walls, voids and compact objects at exact J2000 positions, and a separate ladder of scales that named Laniakea and the Virgo cluster as sizes — and nothing ever asked the positions which structure contains which. The containment arithmetic needs no new number: the positions are in one frame, the extents are declared, and the test is one subtraction and one comparison. CLOSED IN v4.213.0 by running it. The observer comes out inside exactly one structure the atlas will assert, and it is Laniakea, which is Tully, Courtois, Hoffman and Pomarede 2014 re-derived from the atlas`s own coordinates rather than copied from the paper. Four other spheres reach us and all four are refused with written reasons — two because the container declares it does not know its own centre, two because the container is a wall and a sphere of a wall`s long half-extent reaches back past us. Seventy-four containments are asserted, two hundred and seventy-eight overlaps are refused, and thirty-three of thirty-eight declared structures contain nothing this atlas has placed, which is a fact about the catalogue and is published as one

the atlas rendered superclusters, walls, voids, filaments, a reconstructed flow basin and eleven black holes in three dimensions, and placed exactly TWO galaxies: the Milky Way and M31, and those only inside the solar-scale ladder. The structure was everywhere and the constituent was nowhere. CLOSED IN v4.213.0 with forty-two galaxies at exact J2000 positions and published distances, and three Coma members repaired on the way. Fifteen of them carry a measured disc inclination and position angle, which between them fix a disc in three dimensions completely, so those fifteen are drawn as oriented exponential discs rather than balls; the rest are drawn round and the ABSENCE of an orientation is declared instead of filled in. What remains open is coverage and not method: the Local Group has some eighty known members and this places twenty-five of them, and every galaxy beyond about fifty million light years is represented by a cluster marker rather than by itself

three Coma cluster member galaxies were typed `cluster` since they were added, and nothing in the atlas cared, because nothing read the type as anything but a colour and a wireframe. The containment census reads it as CONTAINER, and the first run concluded that the Coma Cluster is inside NGC 4874 — the member sat six ten-thousandths of a gigalightyear from the cluster centre and declared a half-extent of two thousandths. CLOSED IN v4.213.0 by retyping them, giving them real diameters (they had carried a display size four million light years across) and asserting in the boot suite that no galaxy is ever a container. THE GENERAL LESSON IS FILED RATHER THAN THE PARTICULAR FIX: a declaration nothing consumes is not verified by anything, and the atlas has many. The census is now one consumer of the type field, and it found the only three errors in it on its first run

ten structures are typed wall and every one was drawn flattened by the same hard-coded triple: written in THREE places as 1 : 0.5 : 0.35 and in a FOURTH as 1 : 0.45 : 0.25. The same wall was one shape in the cosmic atlas and a different shape in the solar frame, and nothing could notice, because a reader never sees both at once. CLOSED IN v4.222.0 with one table read by all four sites, and the boot suite compares the drawn ratio of every wall across the two layers rather than trusting that they agree. Two structures in the catalogue have all three dimensions published and now carry their measured ratio: the CfA2 Great Wall at 1 : 0.6 : 0.03, a sheet twenty times thinner than the convention drew it, and the Local Sheet at 1 : 1 : 0.15. WHAT IS STILL OPEN, AND IS COUNTED AS ZERO RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE READ OUT OF THE PICTURE: declaring a ratio and then laying it along the scene axes measures the shape and INVENTS the direction. v4.223.0 closed ONE of the ten and could close no more: the Local Sheet is not a wall that happens to lie somewhere, it is DEFINED as the flattened structure in the supergalactic plane, so its normal is the supergalactic pole and the atlas already carries the transform. It is drawn in that plane now. The other nine lay their ratio along the scene axes, and the census counts one asserted orientation rather than ten, so nobody reads a direction out of a picture that has not got one. What would close them is a published position angle and inclination per structure, the way the fifteen oriented galaxies already carry them — and for a wall found in a redshift slice that number is usually not published at all, which is the honest reason the count is likely to stay near one

the census tests |p_object - p_container| against the container`s declared half-extent, and one hundred and thirty of the overlaps it finds come from walls, filaments and survey fields — structures the atlas already draws as flattened ellipsoids, whose long half-extent swung round as a sphere reaches places the structure does not. The South Pole Wall, at half a gigalightyear with a half-extent of 0.685, swallows the observer. Those are recorded as refusals with the reason and never counted as containments, which is honest but is not the measurement anyone wants. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT is a declared orientation and axis ratio for each elongated structure — the atlas already stores an ellipsoid scale for drawing them, and a containment test against that ellipsoid would convert a hundred and thirty refusals into a hundred and thirty answers. It is not done here because the drawn axis ratios are visual conventions rather than published shape parameters, and promoting a rendering constant to a physical claim is the failure this whole register exists to prevent

the other half of the refused overlaps come from containers that declare centroidKnown:false — Lopez field midpoints, reconstruction anchors, the KBC underdensity, the Quipu superstructure track. A sphere drawn around a centre the atlas does not know cannot decide what is inside it, so the census will not assert those memberships. This is a debt with a named remedy and no shortcut: each one closes when a catalogue centroid for that structure is quoted and cited, in the way the atlas already cites the Dipole Repeller`s CF3 location and the South Pole Wall`s density peak. Guessing a centre from the marker that is currently drawn would close the count and destroy the meaning

declaring the wheels of time as an instrument made them askable for the first time, and the first question answered found this: the Chinese sexagenary phase and the Tibetan rabjung phase come back IDENTICAL to the last digit, at every epoch tested across three thousand years. Both turn in sixty years of 365.2422 days, and neither declares an era of its own, so both fall back to the same stipulated instant and the arithmetic cannot tell them apart. That is a gap in the epoch table and not a fact about the calendars: the rabjung is counted from 1027 CE, the year the Kalachakra reckoning begins, and the sexagenary cycle is not. IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT PATCHED. Inventing a Julian day for the rabjung so that two numbers stop agreeing would be manufacturing a source, which is the one move this atlas may not make, and the difference between a wheel that has an era and a wheel that has been given one is invisible in the output. What is done instead is a measurement: a boot assertion compares every pair of wheels that carries a phase at four widely separated epochs and NAMES any pair that agrees to within a millionth of a turn, so this coincidence is on the record and a second one introduced later cannot arrive quietly. What would close it is a sourced rabjung epoch, quoted and cited the way the Goodman-Martinez-Thompson correlation and the era of Nabonassar already are, at which point the assertion turns red on its own and the entry can be deleted rather than argued away

the asteroseismology laboratory publishes four quantities to the runtime bus -- the large frequency separation, the frequency of maximum power, the mean density and the surface gravity -- and not one of them can be routed anywhere, because hccBusLink refuses them with "unknown laboratory". The bus registry is built from DECLARED INSTRUMENT CONTRACTS, and this laboratory has status MODEL with no declared inputs or outputs, so it is invisible to the very bus it publishes into. That is not a defect in either half: a station that draws a relation is a different thing from an instrument that answers a question, and the atlas distinguishes them deliberately. What was open is that nothing SAID so at the point of publication. MEASURED AT LAST, AND THE GAP IS FOUR TIMES WHAT THIS ENTRY GUESSED. ATLAS_BUS.pub now computes a routability verdict and RETURNS it, HCC_BUS_ROUTABILITY() is the census in both directions, the laboratory panel shows every reader which of the values in front of them the bus could carry, and docs/verify-bus-publications-are-routable.cjs runs the atlas`s own busRoutability over the atlas`s own generated contract table and holds the number under a ceiling that only falls. The first honest count: 272 publications, 40 routable, 232 not -- and 1317 declared outputs that nothing publishes at all. Sixty-two of the 232 come from fifteen stations with no contract, which is the case this entry was filed about and the smaller half. THE LARGER HALF WAS NOT SUSPECTED: 170 come from stations that DO hold a contract which calls the same quantity something else. sn.L on the wire against the declared sn.luminosity; bht.TH against bht.T_H; exo.transit_depth_ppm against exo.depth_ppm; rmhd.vA against rmhd.alfven_speed; galrot.rotation_speed against galrot.v_observed. The bus vocabulary and the contract vocabulary are two authorities for one fact across ninety-four laboratories, which is this atlas`s own definition of a defect, and no amount of care at a single publication site would have revealed it -- only counting all of them at once did. What remains open is the repair, and it is deliberately not a rename script: each of the 170 has to be decided one at a time, because a bus name and a contract name that look alike are not thereby the same coordinate, and asserting they are is the exact error the quantity-kind test exists to prevent. THE NARROWER NOTATION DEFECT FILED HERE IS CLOSED: the seismic density was published as "kg/m^3" and the runtime wd.density as "kg/m3" where every declared input writes "kg m^-3". Both now write "kg m^-3" and neither other spelling appears anywhere in the source. The unit half of the routability rule keeps it closed: a publication whose unit is not the declared unit is refused as unit_disagrees rather than counted as a coupling

the resolution laboratory paints its Airy field through min(1,I) and a display gamma, which is correct for a texture that cannot show more than white, and the first version of its dip measurement called the SAME function. The clamp is quietly optimistic about contrast -- nearly four points low where it is worst, and flatly zero at 0.80 Rayleigh limits where the dip is 0.54 per cent -- but that is not the damage worth recording. Bisecting the Sparrow limit through the clamped profile returns 0.300, which is the bottom of the search bracket, because a clamped profile has an EXACTLY flat top whose second derivative is zero rather than negative, so the split test never fires and the bisection walks to its own edge and reports it with every appearance of having converged. A wrong number that looks like a measurement is worse than a missing one, and nothing about the shape of the code said which of the two callers was entitled to the clamp. What stays open is that this atlas has no general separation between a display path and a measurement path: dozens of stations clamp, gamma-correct, quantise to a texel grid or round for a label, and any of those functions can be called by something that wants the physics. No check here distinguishes the two kinds of caller, and the one case that was caught was caught because a bisection collapsed loudly rather than because anything was watching. AND THE OBVIOUS INSTRUMENT FOR IT DOES NOT WORK, which was measured rather than supposed: a census over the 1193 extracted declarations looking for display OPERATIONS -- a clamp to one, a clamp to 255, a rounding, a fractional exponent read as a display gamma -- returns 48 hits of which almost none are the thing. Math.pow(m,0.8) is the mass-radius law of a main-sequence star and not a gamma; Math.min(1,(rs+rp)/a) is a transit probability that genuinely cannot exceed one; a rounding inside a Poisson draw is the discreteness of photons; and the depth-mapping functions it flags are display functions doing exactly what they should. The defect in the resolution laboratory was never that a clamp EXISTED, it was that a measurement CALLED a renderer -- a relation between two functions, not a property of either. So finding it mechanically needs a call graph that knows which sites are drawing and which are measuring, and the atlas has no such labelling; a census over operations will only ever produce a list that has to be read one entry at a time, which is the thing it was supposed to save

the Sparrow limit came out at 0.7766 and the number remembered from the textbooks was 0.947, which looked like a seventeen per cent error and was not an error at all: 0.7766 Rayleigh limits IS 0.9471 lambda over D, and the quoted 0.947 is in lambda/D. The same three digits name two different quantities in two units, and comparing them straight across manufactures a disagreement out of nothing. This is exactly the failure the quantity bus refuses couplings over -- a unit string that does not match means the two are not the same coordinate -- and the bus caught none of it, because neither number ever entered the bus: both lived inside one verifier as bare JavaScript numbers. What stays open is that the bus governs quantities that are PUBLISHED and has no reach into arithmetic, and most of the arithmetic in this atlas is bare numbers in local scope. A unit-carrying numeric type would have caught this at the comparison; there is none here, and no measurement of how many other constants in these verifiers are compared across a unit they do not share

scripts/liveness.mjs measures two things per view -- RECOMPUTED, buffer attributes whose version advanced, and MOVED, objects whose world matrix changed -- and its own header says in capitals that NEITHER IS A VERDICT and that a laboratory meant to be a diagram scores zero on both and is right to. It was read as a verdict anyway. Twenty-five views scoring zero on both were taken for static pictures, ranked by how much geometry sat still, and lined up as the target list for giving every instrument richer motion; the largest, civpa4, carries 291 bodies. The first thing measured was whether the geometry responds to the controls the laboratory declares, and it does: moving civpA changed the scene, so CIVP is event-driven rather than dead and the premise was already wrong. The four least promising were then driven through every control and compared by RENDERED IMAGE rather than by label text, and all four both self-animated and responded. A full walk with the image compared says all twenty-five are alive -- through materials, shaders and inherited rotation, none of which dirties a buffer or moves a watched body. NOTHING IN THE ATLAS WAS INERT. The instrument was careful and the reading was not: two numbers that decline to be a verdict were turned into one by a reader who wanted a target list. What was added is a third, orthogonal reading -- PIXELS, whether the rendered image differs between two frames with nothing touched -- published per view in api/liveness.json and pinned by docs/verify-liveness-artifact.cjs so it cannot quietly vanish. It is not a verdict either, and for the opposite reason to the other two: a view can be alive and momentarily identical, and a view can shimmer while its physics is frozen. What it adds is the one distinction the first two cannot draw, between a diagram that is still by design and a diagram that is still because it broke. WHAT IS OPEN is that none of the three sees whether the motion MEANS anything. A shader advancing a uniform scores alive on pixels exactly as a solved trajectory does, and the atlas has no measure of whether what moves on the screen is the physics or the decoration

the S3 tick is a chain of else-if branches on state.s3view ending in an else that rotates the eigenmode sphere and writes the eigenmode caption. A laboratory whose view matches no branch does not fail -- it silently runs that fallback. Eight did: the seven CIVP laboratories and the Fibonacci anyon laboratory, so a reader standing in A4 transfer was told Eigenmode beta = 4 and had an unrelated sphere rotated on their behalf. For CIVP it cost far more than a caption. updateCivp holds the ONLY publications of civp.residual, civp.delta_lock, civp.index and civp.q_star, and it was called from the nul branch, where civpGroup.visible is false -- so the update ran only where the geometry is hidden and never where it is shown, exactly backwards. The values never left the laboratory that computes them, and the declared coupling civpsel.q_star to civpclo.q could not run from inside either laboratory. Both are fixed and all seven now publish from inside themselves. WHAT THIS ENTRY IS REALLY ABOUT is the measurement that found it and nearly published a false one. A first walk of all 114 laboratories with a 600 ms settle reported 58 distinct captions and sixty laboratories wearing another instrument name; the same walk at 2600 ms reported 112. The 600 ms figure was almost entirely the PREVIOUS laboratory caption, still on screen because the next one had not finished rebuilding. The instrument was wrong, not the subject, and the difference between a defect in eight laboratories and a defect in sixty is the settle time of the harness. WHAT WAS OPEN -- that the fallback is silent by construction, so adding a laboratory without adding a branch produces no error, no warning and a plausible-looking screen -- IS NOW CLOSED. The router chain is delimited by explicit markers and scripts/validate.mjs reads the branch ids between them, compares them against every s3 laboratory in HCC_ATLAS_LAB_META (the same record the routes and the manifest are built from, so neither side can be edited quietly to agree) and fails the build NAMING any laboratory that is not routed. Only eig may be absent, because eig is the laboratory the fallback belongs to. Measured: 112 laboratories, 112 branches, zero unrouted, both mutations caught by name. The first version of the CIVP clause was not caught: it tested for the lookup CIVP_VIEW_STATION[state.s3view] anywhere in the chain, which false && CIVP_VIEW_STATION[state.s3view] still satisfies, so disabling the branch kept the build green; it matches the live branch head now. And a parse that sliced the chain too narrowly had reported thirty-eight unrouted laboratories where there is one -- the same lesson as the settle time, read the whole thing before counting. WHAT REMAINS is that this covers routing, not correctness: a laboratory routed to the wrong update passes every clause here

the phase frame once rendered the hierarchy content instead of its own: its torus was a child of a group the frame hides, so the flag said visible, the object said visible, and the reader saw somebody else scene. The frame-loop walk cannot catch that class. It proves no frame throws and that no two frames draw the SAME label set, and a collapsed frame draws neither -- reverting that fix leaves phase showing seven labels against eighty-eight, a different set, so the distinctness clause passes on the broken page; this was measured by mutation rather than assumed. Two stronger clauses were tried and both were wrong for reasons worth keeping. Comparing labels verbatim counted every time-varying readout as unique, because the atlas clock advances between one frame and the next, so four frames passed on a timestamp. Comparing label SHAPES removed that and then failed helio -- correctly, because helio isolates the seasonal dial that the hierarchy also draws, so a focus view legitimately shows a subset and contributes nothing of its own. "Every frame brings something no other frame has" is false by design in this atlas. WHAT IS OPEN is that the only invariant that would catch it is per-frame: this frame must show the instrument it exists to show. updateCyc knows exactly that, and knows it as control flow -- cycPhaseInst.visible = frame condition, repeated for a dozen instruments -- so nothing outside the function can ask which instrument a frame owes the reader. Declaring the frame-to-instrument map as data, the way HCC_STATIONS declares stations, would make it checkable and would also be the second authority that caught the six unopenable stations. THAT IS NOW DONE. CYC_FRAME_INSTRUMENTS declares which instruments each frame owes the reader and the visibility assignments are made FROM it, so the declaration is load-bearing rather than decorative, and four assignments that duplicated it were deleted. HCC_CYCLE_FRAMES exposes what each frame owes NOW -- each condition evaluated by the runtime rather than described in prose -- beside what is actually on screen, computed as the product over every ancestor. The check compares promise against delivery with nothing skipped, and reverting the phase fix now fails it by name: the phase frame owes cycPhaseInst and cycResonanceInst and neither is on screen. The first version of that clause skipped any entry carrying a condition, and BOTH of the phase frame instruments carry one, so it could not have failed for the only frame it was written for; that was found by mutation and is why the conditions are predicates. WHAT REMAINS is that this covers the cycles laboratory alone. A hundred and thirteen others assign visibility as control flow the same way, and none of them can say what a view owes

verify-verifier-coverage asserted selfContained.length > reading.length -- "most of them never read the atlas" -- and went red the moment the split reached sixty-four and sixty-four, which happened because verifiers that DO read the atlas were added. The check failed for an IMPROVEMENT in the thing it measures. The same file already documents this exact error one clause lower, where an artifact requirement had been written as "at least one artifact must rest on reproduction alone" and broke when every artifact gained a reading verifier; the lesson was written down and then repeated six lines higher in the same file. The fix is the same both times: assert the part that stays true whichever way the number goes -- a self-contained verifier can say what ought to be true and never whether this code does it, and the reading set carries a floor -- and REPORT the split instead of ruling on it. WHAT IS OPEN is that this shape is not detectable by reading a check: an assertion about a current ratio and an assertion about an invariant look identical, and both pass on the day they are written. The only signal is that a check goes red on a change that made the system better, which is indistinguishable at the moment it happens from a check going red on a regression. Every threshold in this suite that was calibrated against the atlas as it stood is a candidate, and nothing enumerates them

three times in one session a check passed while the defect it was written for sat in the file, and all three failed the same way: the expected value came from the thing under test. First, a verifier read globalThis.ATLAS_TELEMETRY, got undefined because the object was module-scoped, coerced it with ||0 and compared zero against zero. Second, a clause asserting that an edge colour is routed from c.exact tested the regex against the WHOLE surrounding block, where c.exact also appears in the opacity line, so hardcoding the pair into the colour still matched. Third, a clause asserting that a declared construction is true computed cycleCommensurability({days:times*base},{days:base}) from the DECLARED multiplier on both sides, which terminates at 1:times for any integer, so changing the declaration from 223 to 224 passed. Each was found only by running the check against deliberately mutated source, and each is now anchored on something the subject cannot supply: the counter must be reachable or the check errors, the colour clause reads only the colour expression, and the declaration is evaluated against the entry own days expression with the kernels in scope. WHAT IS OPEN is that nothing detects this shape mechanically. A check whose expected value is computed from the same source as its actual value is structurally incapable of failing, and it reads exactly like a check that passes. The suite has a hundred and twenty-eight files and the only instrument for finding these is to mutate the source and see which of them notices, which is done by hand, on the file being written, by whoever happens to remember. Every check written before that habit existed is unaudited

tick() wraps the whole frame body in try/catch so a single bad frame can never leave a reader looking at a black screen, logs the first one to the console, and increments ATLAS_TELEMETRY.tickErrors. Every part of that is right. What it also does is convert a hard failure into a permanent quiet one: the Cycles linked-analysis view called fmt() at module scope where no fmt is declared -- five closures in this file each define their own and none of them reaches module scope -- so it threw a ReferenceError on its first readout, EVERY FRAME, from the day it was written. The throw unwound updateCyc before its HUD caption and its bus publications and unwound tickBody before the CSS2D label pass, the hierarchy locator and the XR telemetry. Nothing crashed. The view simply drew nothing new, the labels froze at whatever the previous frame had left, and the page did more work for less result. It was reported from outside as a button that does nothing and a page that had got slower, which is exactly what it was. THE COUNTER EXISTED AND NOTHING READ IT. Worse, the first verifier written for this defect read globalThis.ATLAS_TELEMETRY, got undefined because the object was module-scoped, coerced it with ||0, and PASSED with the defect still in the file; only running it against the mutated source found that. WHAT WAS DONE is the walk: the verifier enters eleven cycle views, seven worlds and ALL ONE HUNDRED AND FOURTEEN laboratories one at a time with rendering on, reading the counter after each so a failure names its laboratory rather than the atlas, and proving the walk moved at all -- fifty-nine distinct scene captions across the hundred and fourteen routes -- because a walk that navigated nowhere would report a clean sweep of a place it never went, which is the exact mistake this entry already records once. WHAT WAS DONE NEXT closed the station gap this entry named, and the gap was hiding a different defect than the one expected. The walk now enters all sixty-one stations declared in HCC_STATIONS as well as the eleven cycle views, the seven worlds and the hundred and fourteen arrivals. Six of those stations could not be entered AT ALL: wind, gyro and seis declare two stations each, the search index is built from that registry so a reader searching their terms is sent to those laboratories, and nothing anywhere assigned state.swStation, state.gyStation or state.seisStation. Their geometry was built on load and hidden on every frame -- three laboratories were half invisible and no exception was ever thrown, so the counter this entry is about would never have found them. The registry supplies the control now for any laboratory that declares stations and has no panel of its own, placed last in the chain so it cannot shadow a hand-written one, and the check requires every declared station to be openable AND to draw something different when opened, since a chip setting a key nothing reads would otherwise pass. WHAT IS STILL OPEN is the counter itself: there is ONE for the whole loop, it says how many frames threw and never where or what, so a failure is localised only to the granularity at which the walk navigates. And the walk is now the coverage: what it does not enter is not checked, and nothing enumerates what it does not enter

the sensitivity sweep gives each declared input a time budget and records how far along its declared drive the budget got. Two consecutive runs of the SAME source, on the same machine, with no physics touched between them, disagree about eleven inputs: ebk.beta_plus reached 54.5 per cent in one run and 45.5 in the next, jonesq.level 45.5 and then 27.3, skyrmion.grid 90.9 and then 81.8. That is expected and it is honestly reported -- a truncated sweep is filed as REFUSED with the percentage named, not as dead. What is not expected is that the boundary itself moves: emb.braid_steps was published as one of the twenty-five DEAD inputs and came back in the next run as refused at 90.9 per cent, so the count fell from twenty-five to twenty-four. It was never dead. It was a sweep slow enough that one run finished it and the next did not, and the class it lands in is decided by how busy the machine was. THE CONSEQUENCE IS THAT A NUMBER THIS ATLAS PUBLISHES IS NOT REPRODUCIBLE. Every statement resting on the dead list -- including the open problem directly below this one, which reasons about exactly twenty-five inputs and the sixteen of them that did not revive -- inherits a denominator that a slower afternoon would have changed. WHAT IS OPEN is that a wall-clock budget is the wrong bound for a classification. Deadness is a claim about the mathematics and it is being decided by a stopwatch. The fix is not more budget, which only moves the threshold: it is a budget counted in evaluations rather than milliseconds, so that two runs of one source see the same samples and can only disagree about the answer

the sensitivity sweep varies one declared input at a time from the atlas own defaults. Twenty-five of 484 moved nothing and the artifact calls them DEAD. The verifier guarding it refuses to call a REFUSED input dead, refuses to call a TRUNCATED sweep dead, keeps the four classes disjoint -- and never asks whether an input that measured dead OUGHT to be. All twenty-five were then driven through the live API in one browser session, each swept at its own extremes and then again with every other input moved off its default, and the answer is in three parts. THREE ARE SILENCED, not dead, and the culprit is named in each case: mainseq.giant_brightening by giant_window_fraction, whose default of zero leaves no window for giants so that a thousand times no light is still no light; skyrmion.separation by the soliton count; scales.drive by the coupling. ONE IS NOT DEAD BY ANY READING: ladder.theta is recorded dead with responding 0 and an empty moves list, while the laboratory own temperature_K runs from 7.778e-18 to 7.778e-8 across the declared domain -- the same mantissa with the exponent ten higher, a clean unit slope over ten decades. An output moving by ten orders of magnitude is recorded as moving nothing. SIXTEEN DID NOT REVIVE at the one alternative co-point each was offered, and that is a statement about the reach of the test rather than a certificate: a single alternative value per co-input is one probe of a space, and inertness would need the space rather than the probe. WHAT IS OPEN is that the sweep publishes an assertion it has no method to support. One-at-a-time from defaults cannot separate an input that does nothing from an input another default has switched off, and the ladder case shows it can also simply miss a response it did sample. Both failures are silent: an input wrongly called dead invites deletion, and the atlas has no second authority on inertness at all

HR_KAPPA sits in this atlas as 0.034 and is used for every Eddington limit it publishes. It is not a number somebody picked: 0.034 is exactly 0.02 times one plus X at X = 0.70, which is the ELECTRON SCATTERING opacity — the one opacity with no metals in it, because a free electron scatters a photon the same way whether it came from hydrogen or from iron. So every Eddington number here is metallicity-blind, which is CORRECT, and it is correct by accident: nothing in the file says which opacity that constant is, so nothing would have objected had it been used where the other one belongs. The identification was made by arithmetic, not by reading intent, and it is now checked. WHAT IS OPEN is that this is a pattern and not an incident. A constant carrying a physical CHOICE — this opacity and not that one, this composition and not another — is indistinguishable in the source from a constant carrying a measurement, and the atlas has many of both. The stellar relations are the sharp case: hrLuminosity, hrRadius and hrTemperature are written for the solar mixture and declare nothing, so the turnoff mass at 1.31 solar, the gyrochronology colour term and the 1.278-against-1.314 coincidence are all composition statements presented as if they were not. Measured rather than asserted: the crossover locus rho_crit = 0.02 T^3.5 / (4e25 Z) puts the Sun 260 times inside the Kramers regime where Z matters and a forty-solar-mass star outside it entirely, so the metallicity sensitivity of a published lifetime depends on which star it is and the atlas states neither. The shape of a fix is a declared composition on the relations that assume one, so that a reader asking for a metal-poor turnoff gets an answer or a refusal rather than a solar number wearing no label

the liveness census counts, per view, how many bodies moved and how much geometry was rebuilt between frames, and it exists to tell an instrument from a picture. A cinematic stage -- a scene-level group of rings, arcs and ticks that declares itself display-only and carries no selectable metric payload -- is a SIBLING of every laboratory, so the traversal handed it to the measurement in every view. That cost nothing while the presentation was opt-in. The moment it became the default, the census reported 150 of 150 views alive: twenty-five laboratories that recompute nothing flipped from still to alive on the same frame, every one of them by moves alone with rebuilds still false, which is the signature of one global change and not of twenty-five laboratories waking up. Measured rather than reasoned: with the presentation off nuc reports 0 bodies moved, with it on 10, and the stage holds exactly ten display layers. The arithmetic never stopped being correct; the instrument simply stopped meaning anything. NOTHING CAUGHT IT except the artifact check that refuses a summary in which everything is alive -- a check that looks like paranoia until the day it fires, and the only reason it fired is that somebody had written down that a census in which every row says the same thing tells nobody anything. WHAT IS OPEN is that the exclusion is now a named reference to one group. Any future scene-level layer -- another stage, a grid, an XR reticle, a shared starfield -- will walk into the same census and devalue it again in exactly the same way, and there is no declared property that says an object is display-only even though the stage itself carries one in prose. The measurement asks the scene graph what is visible when it should be asking what is a laboratory, and until an object can DECLARE that it is not metric, every census over the scene is one default away from measuring the decoration

the Saros is now reached twice: 223 synodic months closing on 242 draconic ones to within 52 minutes, and 19 eclipse years closing on the same interval to within eleven hours. Two independent routes to one number, one counting the MOON back to a node and the other the SUN, and the temptation is to present that as confirmation. It is not: the solar route is 12.7 times looser, because it counts a slow body against a slow cycle and inherits the coarser grain, so averaging the two would make the answer WORSE than the better of them and quoting their agreement would be quoting the precision of the worse one. The laboratory states the ratio rather than the agreement. WHAT IS OPEN is that this atlas has no general treatment of the case. It already refuses couplings whose units disagree and records coincidences it has tested for being accidents, but nothing anywhere carries the PRECISION of a route alongside its answer, so two routes to one quantity arrive as two equal numbers and the reader is left to notice that one of them is worth twelve of the other. The sensitivity sweep knows the slope of every declared input and could carry an error bar; the bus carries values and units and no uncertainty at all. Until it does, every place this atlas reaches one number by two paths is a place where the coarser path can quietly set the credibility of the finer one

the wind laboratory found that mass loss LENGTHENS the main sequence rather than shortening it, and the account written for it was that a wind takes the envelope while the core keeps its hydrogen. Mutation testing found that assumption invisible: a mutant letting the wind eat the fuel changed nothing any check asserted. THE STORY THEN WENT WRONG TWICE MORE, and both corrections are recorded because the sequence is the finding. The commit that followed the mutant declared the core-fuel account did NO work at all, on the strength of that invisibility. It does: neutralised properly through the causal-claims table, removing it cuts the lengthening by a factor of 2.3, against the exponent-steepness account which cuts it by 3.4. BOTH are load-bearing, neither alone, and the exponent carries more. The original prose was too strong, the correction to it was too strong in the other direction, and only the measurement has the right size. THE INSTRUMENT NOW EXISTS: HCC_BECAUSE declares a causal claim as the quantity it holds responsible plus the way to set that quantity aside, and docs/verify-causal-claims.cjs neutralises each named cause and demands the result move — with a synthetic claim whose cause does nothing rejected by the same test, so the passes mean something. WHAT REMAINS OPEN IS THE COVERAGE, and it is now measured rather than guessed: the source carries 1159 causal turns of phrase (870 because, 143 which-is-why, 98 the-reason, 47 so-that, 1 it-follows-that) and five are declared. That 1159 is an UPPER BOUND and not a target: most explain physics in general rather than a result this atlas computes, and only the second kind can be neutralised at all. Separating them mechanically is the same wall the threshold-tolerance and the display-path problems both hit — the claims are prose, and nothing marks which sentence is about a number the atlas produced

the colour at which the spin-down clock diverges is 6880 K, and this atlas`s own mass-luminosity relation reaches that surface temperature at 1.278 solar masses. The nuclear clock puts the turnoff of a 4.57 Gyr population at 1.314. Two limits from a magnetised wind and from a fusion rate, sharing no constant, landing 2.75 per cent apart -- and the honest reading is that the stars gyrochronology refuses are very nearly the stars a solar-age population has already buried. It is also, checked directly, AN ACCIDENT OF THE AGE: the ratio is 1.74 at one billion years and 0.71 at 13.8, sweeping through unity and happening to cross near the age of the Sun. That the check earns its strictness was measured rather than assumed -- against a mutant whose turnoff returns the same mass at every age, so that it is not a clock at all, the strict form fails at 11 of 12 while the form that asserts only the agreement passes 12 of 12. WHAT IS OPEN is that this atlas is full of agreements between independently computed numbers and nothing distinguishes the ones that are physics from the ones that are arithmetic coincidences. The distinguishing test is always the same -- vary a parameter neither side declares and see whether the agreement survives -- and it has been written by hand exactly once, here. It cannot currently be applied mechanically: 39 of the 94 verifiers compare two quantities against a relative tolerance, but that count is a grep over the shape of the expression and not a declared property, and the parameter each agreement would have to be swept in is nowhere named. This is the same architectural wall the threshold-tolerance problem hit from the other side -- the assertions are prose and code rather than declarations naming what they bound -- and the sensitivity sweep, which already varies every declared input of every instrument, is the obvious machine to point at it and cannot be, because verifiers are not instruments and their comparisons are not couplings

the exoplanet laboratory computes every orbit from the measured heliocentric GM and never from G times a solar mass, and the cost of the other route is measured rather than asserted: 257 parts per million in the product and 85 in the semi-major axis, which is thirteen thousand kilometres in the Earth`s orbit. The rule generalises and has NOT been applied across this atlas. Any laboratory that writes G * M where a gravitational parameter is measured directly is importing the twenty-two parts per million of G, and a search for that pattern has not been run. Where the answer is wanted to a per cent it does not matter and most of this atlas wants a per cent; where it does matter nothing currently flags it, and the general form of the check -- a constant that is measured as a product must not be reassembled from its factors -- has no mechanical enforcement here

the three earlier collisions were all inside one laboratory: an input called `steps`, one called `neighbours`, an output called `radius_ratio`. The fourth is different in kind and worse. The galaxy laboratory shipped an input named `mass_to_light`, and it was RIGHT to: the thing it multiplies is a mass-to-light ratio, the name is descriptive, and nothing in the atlas collided with it. One release later the main-sequence laboratory published an output named `mass_to_light` -- also right, also descriptive -- and the two are a MULTIPLIER of 1 and an ABSOLUTE RATIO of 9.4 in solar units. The bus proposed the coupling on a shared name and a shared absence of units, and routing it would have multiplied a galaxy`s stellar mass by nine. What is new is that NEITHER NAME WAS BAD. The earlier three were caught by the rule "do not call an input `steps`"; this one defeats that rule entirely, because both names are the most accurate word available for what they hold and the collision is between two correct choices made a release apart. The refusal is written and the galaxy input is renamed to stellar_mass_multiplier, which is uglier and says what it is. What stays open is that no rule about naming could have prevented this: the atlas would need to know that two dimensionless quantities called the same true thing are a ratio and a multiplier of that ratio, and there is nowhere in the declaration format to say so. A `relative_to` field on dimensionless outputs is the obvious shape of a fix and it is not built. AND THE SAME RELEASE PRODUCED A FIFTH, which defeats that proposed fix as well: the main sequence publishes an eddington_ratio and so do the quasar and the accretion disk. Same name, same units, same formula character-for-character -- L over 4 pi G M c / kappa -- and the names are not generic, not lazy and not renameable, because eddington_ratio is the only correct word for any of them. What differs is the OBJECT: a star burning hydrogen at twenty-six parts per million of its limit, and matter falling onto a black hole at close to unity. No unit expresses that, no name expresses it when the name is right on both sides, and no declared domain expresses it because both values sit inside any plausible range for a fraction. Five collisions, and the fifth is the first that the declaration format could not have caught even in principle.
